from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

import pydantic

from pydantic_ai.native_tools import AbstractNativeTool
from pydantic_ai.tools import AgentDepsT, AgentNativeTool

from .abstract import AbstractCapability

_NATIVE_TOOL_ADAPTER = pydantic.TypeAdapter(AbstractNativeTool)


@dataclass
class NativeTool(AbstractCapability[AgentDepsT]):
    """A capability that registers a native tool with the agent.

    Wraps a single [`AgentNativeTool`][pydantic_ai.tools.AgentNativeTool] — either a static
    [`AbstractNativeTool`][pydantic_ai.native_tools.AbstractNativeTool] instance or a callable
    that dynamically produces one.

    Equivalent to passing the tool through `Agent(capabilities=[NativeTool(my_tool)])`. For
    provider-adaptive use (with a local fallback), see [`NativeOrLocalTool`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.NativeOrLocalTool]
    or its subclasses like [`WebSearch`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.WebSearch].
    """

    tool: AgentNativeTool[AgentDepsT]

    def get_native_tools(self) -> Sequence[AgentNativeTool[AgentDepsT]]:
        return [self.tool]

    @classmethod
    def from_spec(cls, tool: AbstractNativeTool | None = None, **kwargs: Any) -> NativeTool[Any]:
        """Create from spec.

        Supports two YAML forms:

        - Flat: `{NativeTool: {kind: web_search, search_context_size: high}}`
        - Explicit: `{NativeTool: {tool: {kind: web_search}}}`
        """
        if tool is not None:
            validated = _NATIVE_TOOL_ADAPTER.validate_python(tool)
        elif kwargs:
            validated = _NATIVE_TOOL_ADAPTER.validate_python(kwargs)
        else:
            raise TypeError(
                '`NativeTool.from_spec()` requires either a `tool` argument or keyword arguments'
                ' specifying the native tool type (e.g. `kind="web_search"`)'
            )
        return cls(tool=validated)

def _dotenv(*keys: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Read ONLY the named keys from ROOT/.env (git-ignored). The file may hold unrelated secrets; they stay unread."""
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    try:
        for line in (ROOT / ".env").read_text().splitlines():
            k, sep, v = line.partition("=")
            if sep and k.strip() in keys:
                out[k.strip()] = v.strip().strip("'\\"")
    except OSError:
        pass
    return out


_env = _dotenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "GIFT_RESEARCH_MODEL")

"""Research agent: finds real, sourced ideas for ONE craft on the web, for ONE maker.

A small pydantic-ai agent (Gemini + its built-in web search, one structured answer, at most a few model requests).
What it may see: the craft, the occasion, the maker's age group / skill level / restricted tools, what materials
the maker owns, and titles it should not repeat. It never sees names, allergies, photos or the calendar.
What it may NOT decide: safety. Whatever it returns is rewritten into our schema and then passes the same code
checks as every other idea (safety flags derived from the text, age, restricted tools, prices, duplicates, denied
words). Anything that fails is dropped, and what survives is stored as an unverified "found online" idea with its
source link, removable with one click."""
import hashlib
import re
import time
from typing import Literal
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator

from . import config, importer, pairing
from .core import filters
from .core.text import norm
from .db.database import DB
from .motif_discovery import CRAFT_WORDS, DENY, near_duplicate

MAX_IDEAS = 3
MAX_REQUESTS = 6  # model round trips (search + answer) per run
_FIELD = lambda v, n: " ".join(str(v).split())[:n]


class FoundIdea(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str = ""
    materials: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    steps: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    difficulty: Literal["easy", "medium", "hard"] = "medium"
    time_minutes: int = 60
    tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    source_url: str = ""

    @field_validator("title", "description", "source_url", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _clip(cls, v): return _FIELD(v or "", 300)

    @field_validator("materials", "tools", "tags", "steps", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _list(cls, v): return [_FIELD(x, 200) for x in (v or [])][:14]


class Found(BaseModel):
    ideas: list[FoundIdea] = Field(default_factory=list)


class ResearchError(Exception):
    """Something the user can act on; the message is shown as-is."""


def enabled() -> bool:
    return bool(config.GEMINI_API_KEY)

"""Research agent: a fake model stands in for Gemini; the point is what the CODE does with what comes back."""
import json

import pytest
from pydantic_ai.messages import ModelResponse, TextPart
from pydantic_ai.models.function import FunctionModel

from app import config, pipeline, research
from app.core.models import Request
from tests.test_two_tier import PAPER, mk


def idea(title, url, **kw):
    base = {"title": title, "description": "A pretty gift.", "materials": ["colored paper"], "tools": ["scissors"],
            "steps": ["Cut the paper.", "Fold it in half.", "Decorate the front."], "difficulty": "easy",
            "time_minutes": 30, "tags": ["diwali"], "source_url": url}
    return {**base, **kw}


def fake(ideas, seen=None):
    def fn(messages, info):
        if seen is not None:
            seen.append(json.dumps([str(m) for m in messages]))
        return ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart(json.dumps({"ideas": ideas}))])
    return FunctionModel(fn)


def test_good_ideas_are_stored_labelled_and_usable():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"], maker_age="adult")
    out = research.run(d, maker_id=1, craft_id="origami", occasion="Diwali",
                       model=fake([idea("Folded paper diya", "https://example.com/diya")]))
    assert [a["title"] for a in out["added"]] == ["Folded paper diya"] and out["error"] is None
    stored = next(i for i in d.ideas() if i["id"] == out["added"][0]["id"])
    assert stored["source_type"] == "researched" and not stored["verified"] and stored["craft_id"] == "origami"
    assert stored["source_url"] == "https://example.com/diya" and stored["safety_flags"] == []
    # it shows up in a craft-filtered request, labelled as found online
    r = pipeline.suggest(d, Request(recipient_id=1, maker_id=1, occasion="Diwali", only_craft="origami"), None, use_llm=False)
    found = [s for s in r["suggestions"] if s.idea_id == stored["id"]]
    assert found and found[0].trust_label == "online"
    assert d.delete_imported_idea(stored["id"])                                   # removable like an import


def test_unsafe_unsourced_duplicate_and_incomplete_ideas_are_dropped():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"], maker_age="child")
    bad = [
        idea("Hot glue lanterns", "https://example.com/a", tools=["hot glue gun"], steps=["Heat the glue gun.", "Glue.", "Dry."]),
        idea("Candle holder", "https://example.com/b", steps=["Light the candle with a flame.", "Wait.", "Enjoy."]),
        idea("No source diya", ""),
        idea("Plain http diya", "http://example.com/c"),
        idea("Two steps only", "https://example.com/d", steps=["Cut.", "Fold."]),
        idea("Sword origami", "https://example.com/e"),
        idea("Origami butterfly", "https://example.com/f"),                          # already a built-in title
        idea("Paper star", "https://example.com/g"),                                 # the one good idea
    ]
    out = research.run(d, maker_id=1, craft_id="origami", model=fake(bad))
    assert [a["title"] for a in out["added"]] == ["Paper star"] or out["added"] == []
    assert len(out["dropped"]) >= 2
    kept = {a["title"] for a in out["added"]}
    assert not kept & {"Hot glue lanterns", "Candle holder", "No source diya", "Plain http diya", "Two steps only", "Sword origami"}


def test_restricted_tools_and_age_are_enforced_in_code_and_sent_in_the_prompt():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    d.update("makers", 1, restricted_tools=["scissors"])
    seen = []
    out = research.run(d, maker_id=1, craft_id="origami", model=fake([idea("Torn paper art", "https://example.com/h")], seen))
    assert out["added"] == [] and any("scissors" in x for x in out["dropped"])
    assert "scissors" in seen[0] and "maker_age_group" in seen[0]


def test_nothing_personal_is_sent_to_the_model():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"], likes=["secret-hobby"], allergies=["peanut"])
    seen = []
    research.run(d, maker_id=1, craft_id="origami", model=fake([], seen))

The research agent is built and wired in, but I couldn't run it against Gemini. Your key returned "quota exceeded" on every current model I tried (gemini-3.8-flash, 3.5-flash, 3.1-flash-lite and flash-latest). All 105 tests pass, using a fake model in place of Gemini. The server is restarted at http://localhost:8765.

How it works - Where it shows up. After you pick a craft, a "Search the web for more ideas" button appears. A run takes about a minute. - What the agent is. It's a small pydantic-ai agent using Gemini with its built-in web search. It makes at most 6 model requests and returns up to 3 ideas as JSON. - What Gemini sees. It sees the craft, the occasion, the maker's age group and skill level, their restricted tools, the names of the materials they own, and the titles to avoid repeating. It never sees names, allergies, likes or photos. A test checks this. - Safety stays in code. The prompt tells Gemini the age limits and restricted tools, but nothing it returns is trusted. Each idea is rewritten into our format, and the safety flags are worked out from its text. - What gets dropped. Anything that needs a restricted tool, is unsafe for the maker's age, has no https source, is a duplicate or has fewer than 3 steps, or contains denied words or links in the steps. Tests cover these. - What gets saved. Ideas that pass are saved as "found online", with the source link. They're unverified, rank high within their craft, and you can remove them like any import. They keep their written steps. You asked to drop steps only on the generic craft-and-subject ideas. - Limits. 10 runs a day (GIFT_RESEARCH_PER_DAY). If the key is missing, the feature is off and nothing leaves your machine.

About your .env - Key handling: it's git-ignored. The code reads only GEMINI_API_KEY from it (and an optional GIFT_RESEARCH_MODEL). - Other secrets in it: it also holds Supabase and Anthropic keys and others that look like they belong to another project. The code doesn't read them, but you may not want them in this folder.

What I haven't verified - Quota: your key needs available quota (check billing, or try a different key). I defaulted to gemini-3.8-flash, because the older 2.5 models now return "no longer available to new users". - Web search with JSON output: the real calls have never run, so I don't know that this combination works on Gemini. Once the quota works, I'll run one real search and fix whatever it reveals. - Idea quality: web ideas rewritten by a model may be weaker than the fixed recipes, and I haven't checked them.

I'll run one live search as soon as you've fixed the quota. Tell me when it's ready.

The research agent now runs end to end through the app. On the Diwali origami request, Gemini searched the web and saved 3 sourced ideas in about 29 seconds. All 105 tests pass, and the server is on http://localhost:8765.

Which model works - Plain Gemini: gemini-3-flash-preview works on your key, so that's the new default. - Gemini's own search: it returns 429 on every model, so this key's tier doesn't allow it. - Workaround: the agent now searches with DuckDuckGo from this machine and uses Gemini only to read and write. Setting GIFT_RESEARCH_SEARCH=gemini switches back if you upgrade the key. - Old models: the 2.5 models are gone for new keys.

What you'd see I can't take a screenshot, so this is the data behind the page. Open Origami for Diwali and press "Search the web for more ideas": - Button: "Search the web for more ideas" sits in the bar at the top of the craft view and shows "Searching the web… (about a minute)" while it runs. - Result: the cards re-list with the new ones first. - Tag: each new card carries a "found online" tag. - Card content: the card shows time, cost and which of your materials it uses, plus 6 steps and a link to the source page. - Example: "Modular Origami Lantern", 45 min, medium, from thesprucecrafts.com, using colored paper, a marker and card paper you already own, with scissors as the only tool. - Rankings: the web ideas rank above your fixed recipes, because they were found for this exact craft and occasion.

Limits - Steps are vague. The agent reads search snippets and not full pages, so some steps are loose, such as "fold it into a pentagon using the standard folding method". The source link is there for the real instructions. - Unverified: these ideas haven't been checked by a person. - Demo data: the 3 ideas are saved in your demo data. Remove them with the delete link if you don't want them.

On MCP and other search tools Yes, pydantic-ai can connect any MCP server through its MCP capability. Options: - Search servers: Brave, Tavily or Exa MCP. Results are better than DuckDuckGo, which can be blocked or rate-limited, but each needs an API key (free tiers exist) and Node to run. - A page-fetch tool. This is what fixes the vague steps, because the agent could read the whole tutorial page. pydantic-ai has a built-in fetch capability, so no key or MCP is needed. I'd add this first. - A search MCP only if DuckDuckGo proves unreliable.

Bash: cat > app/gallery.py <<'E' """Photos of things the user has made, shown together on the home page. 
cat > app/gallery.py <<'E'
"""Photos of things the user has made, shown together on the home page.

Two sources, merged newest first: photos added straight to the gallery ("I made this"), and the photo of a
finished gift from a plan. Uploads go through the same re-encoding as every other image (EXIF/GPS dropped)."""
import time

from . import importer
from .db.database import DB


class GalleryError(ValueError):
    """A problem the user can fix; the message is shown as-is."""


def add(db: DB, photo: bytes, *, title: str = "", note: str = "", idea_id: str = "") -> int:
    if not photo:
        raise GalleryError("Choose or take a photo first.")
    try:
        name = importer.store(importer.sanitise(photo)[0])
    except importer.InputError as e:
        raise GalleryError(str(e))
    cur = db.conn.execute("INSERT INTO creations(title,note,photo,idea_id,created) VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)",
                          (title.strip()[:80], note.strip()[:300], name, idea_id[:80], time.time()))
    db.conn.commit()
    return cur.lastrowid


def items(db: DB, limit: int = 60) -> list[dict]:
    made = [{"kind": "made", "id": r["id"], "title": r["title"], "note": r["note"], "photo": r["photo"],
             "created": r["created"], "for": ""} for r in db.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM creations")]
    gifts = [{"kind": "gift", "id": r["id"], "title": r["title"] or "A gift", "note": r["note"], "photo": r["photo"],
              "created": r["date"], "for": r["name"] or ""}
             for r in db.conn.execute("SELECT g.id,g.note,g.photo,g.date,r.name,g.idea_id,"
                                      "(SELECT json_extract(data,'$.title') FROM ideas WHERE id=g.idea_id) AS title "
                                      "FROM gifts g LEFT JOIN recipients r ON r.id=g.recipient_id WHERE g.photo!=''")]
    return sorted(made + gifts, key=lambda x: -x["created"])[:limit]


def delete(db: DB, creation_id: int) -> bool:
    row = db.conn.execute("SELECT photo FROM creations WHERE id=?", (creation_id,)).fetchone()
    if not row:
        return False
    db.conn.execute("DELETE FROM creations WHERE id=?", (creation_id,))
    db.conn.commit()
    importer.delete_images([row["photo"]])
    return True

js='''/* Shared by every page: helpers, the page shell (header + tabs + footer), icons. No network except this app's own API. */
const $=id=>document.getElementById(id), L=s=>s.split(',').map(x=>x.trim()).filter(Boolean);
const esc=s=>String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g,c=>({'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;',"'":'&#39;'}[c]));
const api=(p,o)=>fetch('/api'+p,o).then(async r=>{if(!r.ok){const j=await r.json().catch(()=>({}));
  throw new Error(typeof j.detail==='string'?j.detail:(j.detail?.[0]?.msg||r.statusText))}return r.status===204?null:r.json()});
const post=(p,b)=>api(p,{method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify(b)});
const put=(p,b)=>api(p,{method:'PUT',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify(b)});
let tt;function toast(m){const t=$('toast');t.textContent=m;t.classList.add('show');clearTimeout(tt);tt=setTimeout(()=>t.classList.remove('show'),2800)}
const guard=f=>async(...a)=>{try{await f(...a)}catch(e){toast(e.message)}};
const I=(n)=>`<svg class="i"><use href="#i-${n}"/></svg>`;
const dayWord=n=>n===0?'today':n===1?'tomorrow':`in ${n} days`;
const fmtDate=d=>new Date(d+'T00:00').toLocaleDateString(undefined,{day:'numeric',month:'short'});
const money=c=>c?` · ₹${c}`:'';
const photo=x=>x.photo_path?`<img src="/photos/${esc(x.photo_path)}" alt="">`:'';
const qs=new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const ideasLink=(rec,occ,go)=>`/ideas?${new URLSearchParams({...(rec?{rec}:{}),...(occ?{occ}:{}),go:go||'crafts'})}`;

const SPRITE=`__SPRITE__`;
const TABS=[['/','home','Home'],['/ideas','sparkle','Find ideas'],['/add','camera','Add ideas'],['/plans','gift','My plans'],
  ['/calendar','clock','Calendar'],['/profiles','heart','Profiles']];
(function shell(){
  const b=document.body, page=b.dataset.page||'';
  b.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin',`<svg width="0" height="0" style="position:absolute" aria-hidden="true"><defs>${SPRITE}</defs></svg>`);
  $('shell').innerHTML=`<header><span class="logo"><svg class="i" style="width:1em;height:1em;stroke-width:1.6"><use href="#i-gift"/></svg></span>
   <div><h1>Gift Bulb</h1><small>cosy handmade gift ideas from what you already have</small></div><span id="status">checking helper…</span></header>
   <nav class="tabs" aria-label="pages">${TABS.map(([h,i,t])=>`<a href="${h}" class="${(h==='/'?page==='home':h==='/'+page)?'on':''}">${I(i)} ${t}</a>`).join('')}</nav>
   ${b.dataset.title?`<h2 class="page-title">${esc(b.dataset.title)}</h2>`:''}${b.dataset.sub?`<p class="page-sub">${esc(b.dataset.sub)}</p>`:''}`;
  b.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend',`<footer><a href="/api/export" download="gift-bulb-backup.json" title="Everything you entered, as one file">Download my data</a> · ${I('home')} Runs on your computer · nothing leaves it except the optional web search</footer>
   <div id="toast"></div><div id="lightbox" onclick="this.classList.remove('show')"><img alt=""></div>`);
  api('/health').then(h=>$('status').innerHTML=h.llm_up?`<span class="dot on"></span>helper ready · ${esc(h.model)}`:`<span class="dot"></span>${esc(h.hint||'helper offline')}`).catch(()=>$('status').textContent='server unreachable');
})();
const zoom=src=>{const l=$('lightbox');l.querySelector('img').src=src;l.classList.add('show')};
'''.replace('__SPRITE__',sprite.replace('`','\\`'))

All six pages load their data from the live server. Next the gallery upload, tested end to end, with tests added.

Bash: cat > tests/test_gallery.py <<'E' import io from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from PIL impo
cat > tests/test_gallery.py <<'E'
import io

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from PIL import Image

from app import gallery, plans
from app.db.database import DB


def jpg(color="red"):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    Image.new("RGB", (40, 30), color).save(buf, "JPEG")
    return buf.getvalue()


def test_add_list_delete_and_bad_upload(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from app import config
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "PHOTOS_DIR", tmp_path)
    d = DB(":memory:")
    cid = gallery.add(d, jpg(), title="Paper star", note="for Maa")
    items = gallery.items(d)
    assert [i["title"] for i in items] == ["Paper star"] and items[0]["kind"] == "made"
    assert (tmp_path / "ideas" / items[0]["photo"]).exists()
    for bad in (b"", b"not an image"):
        try:
            gallery.add(d, bad)
            assert False
        except gallery.GalleryError:
            pass
    assert gallery.delete(d, cid) and not gallery.delete(d, cid) and gallery.items(d) == []
    assert not (tmp_path / "ideas" / items[0]["photo"]).exists()


def test_finished_gift_photos_appear_with_the_recipient(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from app import config
    from tests.test_two_tier import PAPER, mk
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "PHOTOS_DIR", tmp_path)
    d = mk(PAPER)
    pid = plans.create(d, recipient_id=1, maker_id=1, idea_id="origami-lotus-diya", occasion="diwali")
    plans.finish(d, pid, rating=5, note="she loved it", photo=jpg("blue"))
    gallery.add(d, jpg(), title="Mine")
    items = gallery.items(d)
    assert {i["kind"] for i in items} == {"made", "gift"}
    gift = next(i for i in items if i["kind"] == "gift")
    assert gift["for"] == "R" and gift["title"]


def test_pages_and_gallery_endpoint_are_served(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("GIFT_DB", str(tmp_path / "t.db"))
    from app import config
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "PHOTOS_DIR", tmp_path)
    from app.main import app
    with TestClient(app) as c:
        for path in ("/", "/ideas", "/add", "/plans", "/calendar", "/profiles"):
            r = c.get(path)
            assert r.status_code == 200 and "Gift Bulb" in r.text and "/assets/js/common.js" in r.text, path
        assert c.get("/assets/css/style.css").status_code == 200
        r = c.post("/api/gallery", files={"photo": ("a.jpg", jpg(), "image/jpeg")}, data={"title": "Hello"})
        assert r.status_code == 201
        assert [i["title"] for i in c.get("/api/gallery").json()] == ["Hello"]
        assert c.post("/api/gallery", files={"photo": ("a.txt", b"nope", "text/plain")}).status_code == 422
        assert c.delete(f"/api/gallery/{r.json()['id']}").status_code == 204

The site is now split into six pages, with a dashboard home page and a photo board for the things you've made. All 108 tests pass (3 new), and every page loaded its data from the live server in a scripted test. I haven't opened it in a real browser, so I can't confirm how it looks.

What changed - Files. app/web/ now has one HTML file per page. A shared stylesheet is in assets/css/style.css. Scripts are in assets/js/: one shared common.js with the header, tabs, icons and helpers, plus one script per page. The old single page is gone. - Tabs. A tab bar runs across the top of every page.

The pages

Page Address What's on it
Home / The dashboard: reminders to start gifts, the next 6 dates, your top 3 gift plans, and the photo board
Find ideas /ideas The pick-a-craft flow, with Drop, Load more, "More " and web search
Add ideas /add Photo import, your saved finds, and the fresh subjects with + and ×
My plans /plans Start-by dates, the make checklist and timer, the shopping list, and gift history
Calendar /calendar The calendar import, your upcoming dates, the "Who for?" picker and the reminder lead time
Profiles /profiles Your basket, recipients and makers, all editable

Links between pages - A reminder or calendar entry opens Find ideas with the person and occasion already filled in. - "Plan this" now shows a link to My plans.

The photo board - Uploading. The home page has an "I made something" button and a photo field. On a phone, the field opens the camera. - How photos show. Each photo is pinned on the board like a polaroid. You can click one to enlarge it, and remove it with ×. - Photos from finished gifts. A photo you add when you finish a gift from a plan also appears on the board, labelled with who it was for. The Plans page's file field opens the camera too. - Privacy. Uploads are re-saved as plain JPEGs, which drops any location data.

Limits - The layout is untested on a real screen, and the phone camera is untested. - The 2-column home layout collapses to 1 column below 760px. - The old page's "More ideas" and "Search the web" buttons moved over unchanged, so their behaviour is as before. - Open http://localhost:8765 and tell me what looks cluttered or wrong.

import http.server,urllib.request,time,sys
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self,*a): pass
    def do_GET(self):
        if self.path=='/slow.css':
            time.sleep(4); self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type','text/css'); self.end_headers(); return
        r=urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8765'+self.path); body=r.read(); ct=r.headers.get('Content-Type','')
        if 'text/html' in ct: body=body.replace(b'<head>',b'<head><link rel="stylesheet" href="/slow.css">',1)
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type',ct); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(body)
http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1',9000),H).serve_forever()

        r = c.post("/api/recipients", json={"name": "Zed Test", "likes": ["ribbons"]}).json()

class FakeLLM:

    model = "fake"

I've redesigned the whole app around your inspiration images. I screenshotted all six pages in headless Firefox and fixed what showed up. All 108 tests pass, and the server is running at http://localhost:8765.

What I took from each image - "I Made IT!" and Craftbox: solid mustard, cobalt and coral blocks, serif headings, a yellow brush stroke behind each page title, and a photo grid. - bg1 and bg2: the hero is a deep blue-green grunge with confetti paper strips (pink, coral, lime, orange, sky and teal) scattered across it. - Feathers and supplies: the mustard-yellow and pop colours carry through the whole app. - Drawn in CSS: I drew all of this in CSS and did not use your photos. The app stays self-contained and doesn't reuse stock images.

What changed - Layout: a clean white top bar with the tabs, then the hero with a torn-paper edge, then white cards on warm cream. The footer is kraft paper. - Colours: the wood theme is gone. Each card has a colour bar (cobalt, mustard, coral, teal, pink), chips and tags come in confetti colours, and each page has its own accent. - Buttons: cobalt, mustard and coral blocks with a torn bottom edge. Secondary buttons are outlined pills. - Photo board: your finished crafts show as colourful polaroids with titles and dates. When it's empty, dashed placeholder tiles show instead. Each tile can be enlarged by clicking. - Dark mode: I removed it. The palette is built for a light background.

What I fixed along the way - Craft grid: the cards were stuck in one column, so they now fill the page width. - Status pill: it was wrapping onto a second line. - Wrapping: tag text was wrapping mid-label. - Database isolation: my earlier tests could write to your real database, because the file path was fixed at import time. Tests now use temporary storage and never touch your data.

Still not checked - Real browser: I looked at it through screenshots only. Hovering, camera upload on a phone, and the narrow mobile layout are untested. - Fonts: headings use Rockwell-style fonts, falling back to Georgia. They look different on other computers. - Button rows: the five action buttons on each idea card still wrap onto two lines.

Reload http://localhost:8765 and tell me which colours, shapes or pages feel off.

@router.get("/health")
def health(r: HttpRequest):
    c = llm(r)
    up = c.available()

    hint = None

def _full(d, table, id_):
    row = d.get(table, id_)
    if row and table == "makers":
        row["skills"] = d.skills(id_)
    return row


def _crud(name: str, table: str, model, extra=None):
    @router.get(f"/{name}")
    def list_(r: HttpRequest):
        rows = db(r).all(table)
        if table == "makers":
            for m in rows: m["skills"] = db(r).skills(m["id"])
        return rows

    @router.post(f"/{name}", status_code=201)
    def add(item: model, r: HttpRequest):
        fields = item.model_dump(exclude={"skills"})
        for k in ("nearby_buyable",):
            if k in fields: fields[k] = int(fields[k])
        id_ = db(r).insert(table, **fields)
        if extra: extra(db(r), id_, item)
        return _full(db(r), table, id_)

    @router.put(f"/{name}/{{id_}}")
    def edit(id_: int, item: model, r: HttpRequest):
        if not db(r).get(table, id_):
            raise HTTPException(404, "not found")
        fields = item.model_dump(exclude={"skills"})
        for k in ("nearby_buyable",):
            if k in fields: fields[k] = int(fields[k])
        db(r).update(table, id_, **fields)
        if extra: extra(db(r), id_, item)
        return _full(db(r), table, id_)

    @router.delete(f"/{name}/{{id_}}", status_code=204)
    def rm(id_: int, r: HttpRequest): db(r).delete(table, id_)

1	# Craft-Idea Agent: Build Plan
2	
3	An agent that suggests craft projects that are doable yet mildly challenging, using maker and recipient profiles, available tools and materials, and photos of past and in-progress work to estimate skill level.
4	
5	**Stack:** Python, `google-genai` (Gemini API), FastAPI, SQLite, Pydantic, Telegram bot for the first interface.
6	
7	**Guiding rules**
8	- The LLM extracts observations and explains choices. Deterministic Python does the skill updates and ranking math.
9	- Every vision output carries confidence scores; low confidence triggers a question to the maker, not a guess.
10	- Start with ONE craft (e.g. knitting or paper crafts) and hand-build its technique taxonomy.
11	- Verify current Gemini model names, rate limits and tool-mixing rules in the official docs before relying on them.
12	
13	---
14

16	
17	- [ ] Create repo, virtualenv, `.env` for the Gemini API key
18	- [ ] Install `google-genai`, `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `pydantic`, `python-telegram-bot`, `requests`, `beautifulsoup4`
19	- [ ] Check the Gemini models page and pick: a fast/cheap model (photo analysis, idea normalizing) and a stronger one (planner, explanations)
20	- [ ] Smoke test: send one image plus a prompt, get a response
21	
22	**Done when:** a script returns a Gemini description of a craft photo.

29	- [ ] Seed script and a few synthetic personas (beginner, intermediate, advanced)
30	
31	**Done when:** you can create a maker, give them inventory, and set a skill estimate per technique.
32

35	- [ ] Prompt plus JSON schema that returns: craft type, finished vs WIP, techniques visible, quality signals (evenness, symmetry, finishing, tension), tools and materials recognized, confidence per field
36	- [ ] Validate with Pydantic; retry once on invalid JSON
37	- [ ] Store the structured analysis with each image so it is never re-analyzed

"""Minimal client for any OpenAI-compatible local server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp). No API key."""
import base64
import json
import re
import time

import httpx

from .. import config

_VISION = ("vl", "vision", "llava", "minicpm-v", "gemma3")
_SKIP = ("vl", "vision", "embed", "llava", "moondream")  # for TEXT work: vision/embedding models are slow or unusable


class LLMError(Exception):
    pass


class LLMClient:
    def __init__(self, base_url: str = config.LLM_BASE_URL, model: str = config.LLM_MODEL,
                 timeout: float = config.LLM_TIMEOUT_S, vision_model: str = config.VISION_MODEL):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.model = model
        self.vision_model = vision_model
        self.timeout = timeout
        self._http = httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(timeout, connect=2.0))
        self._up_checked = 0.0
        self._up = False

    # ---- discovery -------------------------------------------------------
    def installed(self) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
        """[(name, size_bytes)]; size 0 when the server doesn't report it."""
        root = self.base_url.removesuffix("/v1")
        try:
            r = self._http.get(f"{root}/api/tags", timeout=2.0)
            if r.status_code == 200:
                return [(m["name"], m.get("size", 0)) for m in r.json().get("models", [])]
            r = self._http.get(f"{self.base_url}/models", timeout=2.0)
            return [(m["id"], 0) for m in r.json().get("data", [])]
        except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError, KeyError):
            return []

    def available(self) -> bool:
        if time.time() - self._up_checked > 10:
            self._up = bool(self.installed())
            self._up_checked = time.time()
        return self._up

    def resolve_model(self) -> str | None:
        """Configured model, else the smallest installed text model (fastest on CPU)."""
        if self.model:
            return self.model
        cands = [(s or 10**12, n) for n, s in self.installed() if not any(k in n.lower() for k in _SKIP)]
        if cands:
            self.model = min(cands)[1]
        return self.model or None

    def resolve_vision_model(self) -> str | None:
        """Configured vision model, else the smallest installed one that can read images."""
        if self.vision_model:
            return self.vision_model
        cands = [(s or 10**12, n) for n, s in self.installed() if any(k in n.lower() for k in _VISION)]
        if cands:
            self.vision_model = min(cands)[1]
        return self.vision_model or None

    # ---- chat ------------------------------------------------------------
    def chat_json(self, system: str, user: str, *, max_tokens: int = config.LLM_MAX_TOKENS,
                  images: list[bytes] | None = None, timeout: float | None = None) -> dict:
        if images:
            model = self.resolve_vision_model()
            if not model:
                raise LLMError("no vision model installed (try: ollama pull qwen2.5vl:7b)")
            content = [{"type": "text", "text": user}] + [
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(b).decode()}}
                for b in images]
        else:
            model = self.resolve_model() or self.resolve_vision_model()
            content = user
        if not model:
            raise LLMError("no suitable local model installed (try: ollama pull qwen2.5:3b)")
        timeout = timeout or self.timeout
        try:

"""Gemini access for the whole backend, built for the FREE tier.

Free keys have small per-minute and per-day request limits and no Google Search grounding, so every model request
passes through one QuotaGuard: a sliding one-minute window, a daily counter that survives restarts, and a cooldown
after a 429. When the guard says no, callers get a friendly LLMError and fall back to the offline rules."""
import asyncio
import threading
import time
from collections import deque

from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelHTTPError, UsageLimitExceeded
from pydantic_ai.models.wrapper import WrapperModel

from .. import config
from ..llm.client import LLMError, parse_json


class QuotaError(LLMError):
    pass


class QuotaGuard:
    def __init__(self, store=None, per_minute: int | None = None, per_day: int | None = None):
        self.store = store  # anything with get_setting/set_setting (the DB); None = in-memory only
        self.per_minute = per_minute or config.GEMINI_PER_MINUTE
        self.per_day = per_day or config.GEMINI_PER_DAY
        self.window: deque[float] = deque()
        self.cooldown_until = 0.0
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self._mem_day = ("", 0)

    # ---- the daily counter ----
    def _day(self) -> tuple[str, int]:
        today = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        raw = self.store.get_setting("gemini_day") if self.store else ""
        day, n = (raw.split("|") + ["0"])[:2] if raw else self._mem_day
        return (today, 0) if day != today else (today, int(n))

    def _bump_day(self) -> None:
        day, n = self._day()
        self._mem_day = (day, n + 1)
        if self.store:
            self.store.set_setting("gemini_day", f"{day}|{n + 1}")

    def used_today(self) -> int:
        return self._day()[1]

    def left_today(self) -> int:
        return max(0, self.per_day - self.used_today())

    def usable(self) -> bool:
        """Cheap check, no network: key present, daily budget left, not cooling down after a 429."""
        return bool(config.GEMINI_API_KEY) and self.left_today() > 0 and time.time() >= self.cooldown_until

    # ---- one request ----
    def reserve(self) -> float:
        """-> seconds to wait before the request may go out. Raises QuotaError when it never may today."""
        with self.lock:
            now = time.time()
            if self.left_today() <= 0:
                raise QuotaError(f"The free Gemini budget for today ({self.per_day} requests) is used up. It resets tomorrow.")
            if now < self.cooldown_until:
                raise QuotaError("Gemini asked us to slow down. Try again in a minute.")
            while self.window and now - self.window[0] > 60:
                self.window.popleft()
            wait = 0.0 if len(self.window) < self.per_minute else 60 - (now - self.window[0]) + 0.05
            if wait > config.GEMINI_MAX_WAIT_S:
                raise QuotaError("Too many requests this minute for the free plan. Try again in a moment.")
            self.window.append(now + wait)
            self._bump_day()
            return wait

    def penalise(self, seconds: float = 65.0) -> None:
        self.cooldown_until = time.time() + seconds


class GuardedModel(WrapperModel):
    """Every real request to Gemini goes through the guard."""

    def __init__(self, wrapped, guard: QuotaGuard):
        super().__init__(wrapped)
        self.guard = guard

    async def request(self, messages, model_settings, model_request_parameters):
        wait = self.guard.reserve()
        if wait:
            await asyncio.sleep(wait)
        try:
            return await self.wrapped.request(messages, model_settings, mod

"""The planner: one pydantic-ai agent that turns a chat message into rule-checked gift ideas.

The loop is bounded (few model requests, few tool calls, a daily free-tier budget) and every answer is validated
against AgentReply. Idea cards shown to the user are the ones the suggest_ideas tool returned, so the model can
never put an unchecked idea in front of someone. If Gemini is unavailable the same rules run without the model."""
import json

from pydantic_ai import Agent, UsageLimits

from .. import config, pipeline

from .tools import TOOLS, AgentReply, Deps

KEEP_RUNS = 2  # earlier chat turns sent back to the model (free-tier tokens are limited)

INSTRUCTIONS = """You are the Gift Bulb helper: you help someone choose and plan a HANDMADE gift they can make with what they already have.
How to work:
- Use tools to look things up. Never invent a project, an idea_id, a price, a date or a rule. Ideas come only from suggest_ideas (or saved online ideas).
- If you don't know who the gift is for or who is crafting, call list_profiles; if still unclear, ask ONE short question instead of guessing.
- To suggest, call suggest_ideas (optionally with a craft_id from list_crafts). Safety, allergies, age, skill, tools and budget are already enforced by it; never argue with its results.
- Prefer ideas that fit the person's learned taste, the occasion and the maker's skill. Explain the pick in one or two friendly sentences.
- Use search_ideas / fetch_page / save_online_idea only when the user asks to look online or the built-in ideas don't fit. Save at most 2 ideas, in your own words, always with the https source.
- Use plan_gift only when the user clearly asks to plan or schedule a specific idea. Use note_preference only for things the user states.
- Be brief and warm. At most one emoji. No step-by-step instructions: link a tutorial with find_tutorial instead.
- In AgentReply put at most 5 idea_ids, copied exactly from suggest_ideas results."""


def build_agent(model) -> Agent:
    return Agent(model, deps_type=Deps, output_type=AgentReply, instructions=INSTRUCTIONS, tools=TOOLS, retries=1)


def _load_history(db: DB, session: str):
    rows = db.conn.execute("SELECT messages FROM agent_runs WHERE session=? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?", (session, KEEP_RUNS)).fetchall()
    msgs = []
    for r in reversed(rows):
        msgs += ModelMessagesTypeAdapter.validate_json(r["messages"])
    return msgs


def forget(db: DB, session: str = "main") -> None:
    db.conn.execute("DELETE FROM agent_runs WHERE session=?", (session,))
    db.conn.commit()


def _fallback(db: DB, why: str, recipient_id, maker_id, occasion: str, message: str) -> dict:
    """No Gemini (no key, budget used up, offline): the same rules, without the model's conversation."""
    out = {"reply": why, "suggestions": [], "questions": [], "actions": [], "fallback": True}
    if not (recipient_id and maker_id):
        out["reply"] += " Pick who the gift is for and who is crafting, and I can still show rule-checked ideas."

    res = pipeline.suggest(db, Request(recipient_id=recipient_id, maker_id=maker_id, occasion=occasion), None, use_llm=False)
    out["suggestions"] = res["suggestions"]
    out["reply"] += " Meanwhile, here are ideas picked by the built-in rules."
    return out

        d = ctx.deps

"""The planner agent, with a scripted fake model standing in for Gemini. What matters is what the CODE guarantees."""
import json
import time

import pytest
from pydantic_ai.messages import ModelResponse, TextPart, ToolCallPart, ToolReturnPart
from pydantic_ai.models.function import FunctionModel

from app import config
from app.agent import planner
from app.agent.gemini import GuardedModel, QuotaError, QuotaGuard
from tests.test_two_tier import PAPER, mk


def scripted(steps):
    """steps: callables(messages, info) -> list[parts]; one per model request, the last one repeats."""
    calls = []

    def fn(messages, info):
        i = min(len(calls), len(steps) - 1)
        calls.append(1)
        return ModelResponse(parts=steps[i](messages, info))
    m = FunctionModel(fn)
    m.calls = calls
    return m


def tool(name, **args):
    return lambda messages, info: [ToolCallPart(name, args)]


def returned(messages, name):
    for m in reversed(messages):
        for p in getattr(m, "parts", []):
            if isinstance(p, ToolReturnPart) and p.tool_name == name:
                return p.content
    return None


def final(message="Here you go", ids=None, questions=()):
    def step(messages, info):
        got = returned(messages, "suggest_ideas")
        use = ids if ids is not None else [i["idea_id"] for i in (got or {}).get("ideas", [])][:3]
        return [ToolCallPart(info.output_tools[0].name, {"message": message, "idea_ids": use, "questions": list(questions)})]
    return step


def guard():
    return QuotaGuard(None, per_minute=100, per_day=1000)


def test_a_grounded_answer_shows_the_cards_the_tool_returned():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    m = scripted([tool("suggest_ideas", occasion="birthday"), final()])
    out = planner.chat(d, guard(), "something for her birthday", recipient_id=1, maker_id=1, model=m)
    assert not out["fallback"] and out["suggestions"] and out["reply"] == "Here you go"
    assert all(s.idea_id for s in out["suggestions"]) and len(m.calls) == 2


def test_an_answer_without_looking_anything_up_is_sent_back_and_retried():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    m = scripted([final(ids=[]), tool("suggest_ideas"), final()])  # 1st: no tools used -> validator retries
    out = planner.chat(d, guard(), "ideas?", recipient_id=1, maker_id=1, model=m)
    assert out["suggestions"] and len(m.calls) == 3


def test_invented_idea_ids_never_reach_the_user():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    m = scripted([tool("suggest_ideas"), final(ids=["made-up-idea"]), final()])
    out = planner.chat(d, guard(), "ideas?", recipient_id=1, maker_id=1, model=m)
    assert out["suggestions"] and all(s.idea_id != "made-up-idea" for s in out["suggestions"])


def test_a_clarifying_question_is_allowed_without_tools():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    m = scripted([final(message="Who is it for?", ids=[], questions=["Who is the gift for?"])])
    out = planner.chat(d, guard(), "I need a gift", model=m)
    assert out["questions"] == ["Who is the gift for?"] and out["suggestions"] == []


def test_safety_rules_still_decide_what_the_agent_can_show():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"], allergies=["wool"], maker_age="child")
    m = scripted([tool("suggest_ideas", occasion="christmas"), final()])
    out = planner.chat(d, guard(), "christmas gift", recipient_id=1, maker_id=1, model=m)
    for s in out["suggestions"]:
        assert "wool" not in " ".join(s.materials_have + s.materials_to_buy).lower()
        assert not {"hot_glue", "knife", "flame", "sewing_needle", "heat", "sharp"} & set(s.safety_flags or [])


def test_write_tools_only_do_what_they_say():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    m = scripted([tool("note_preference", recipient_id=1, kind="like", item="tulips"),
                  tool("suggest_ideas"), final()])
    out = planner.chat(d, guard(), "she loves tulips", recipient_id=1, maker_id=1, model=m)
    assert "tulips" in d.get("recipients", 1)["likes"] and out["actions"][0]["t

The backend now runs through a pydantic-ai agent on your free Gemini key, and all 120 tests pass. I did the conversion part of plan.md. The new features beyond it need your yes first.

What's built - Planner agent. There's an "Ask the helper" chat box on the Find ideas page and a POST /api/agent/chat endpoint. The agent has 14 tools wrapping the existing rules: profiles, inventory, craft options, rule-checked suggestions, scoring, calendar, shopping list, tutorial link, planning, web search and page reading. - Grounded answers. The model can't invent an idea, because the idea cards it shows must have come back from the suggestion tool. A validator sends back any answer that skipped the tools or used an unknown idea id. The strict rules (safety, allergies, age, skill, restricted tools, budget, repeats) still decide what appears. - Memory. Profiles and calendar are untouched. I added one table that keeps the last 2 chat turns per session. - Every model feature now runs on Gemini. That covers personalised text, card messages, new subjects and photo reading, all through one shared client. The local model is only a fallback when there's no key.

Feature Local model Gemini
Personalised text about 60 s 5 s
Photo reading about 2 min about 9 s

Free-tier handling - Models. Your key allows only 5 requests per minute on the full flash models, so I defaulted to gemini-3.5-flash-lite, which took bursts of 7 or more. - Guard. Every request goes through one guard: 10 per minute and 150 per day, both configurable, with the daily count saved across restarts. It waits out Gemini's own retry delay after a 429. - Offline fallback. If Gemini is out of quota or unavailable, the chat answers with rule-based ideas and says so. A typical run uses 1 to 3 requests, and 28 of today's 150 are used so far. - Search. Google's own search needs a paid plan, so the agent searches through DuckDuckGo.

Limits - Tool use. The lite model once skipped the tools entirely. The validator fixed that in testing, at the cost of an extra request. - Chat quality. I tested a few chats and looked at one reply. I haven't judged quality over many conversations. - Not done: the profile pages from your earlier request are only started.

Needs your yes before I build it These are the plan.md items beyond conversion. Which should I do? 1. Skill model. Skills per craft with a confidence score, updated from finished projects and photos, using your finished-project photos on the board. 2. Technique taxonomy. A list of techniques for one craft, so ideas can be scored as "mostly known plus 1 to 2 new things". 3. Feedback loop. After each project, a too-easy / right / too-hard question that recalibrates skill. 4. Profile pages. Taste profile, maker skills and per-person dates, as you chose earlier. 5. Telegram bot. It needs a bot token, so it's not free to skip setup.

Before building, a straight answer on Telegram, since you asked why we'd need it. We don't. Everything it would do already works in the web app, which runs on a phone browser (the photo field opens the camera). The one real gain is push reminders, because the web page can only remind you when it's open. I'll build everything else now, and leave Telegram as an optional extra for reminders only if you want it.

"""The skill model. Deterministic Python does ALL the maths; the model only supplies observations.

Each maker has, per technique, a level on the 0-5 tier scale and a confidence 0-1.
  prior      : the maker's own 0-3 self-report for the craft, with low confidence
  evidence   : finished projects, photo analyses (weighted by their confidence, WIP counts more), and difficulty reports
  rule       : good work lifts the level toward the technique's tier; visibly rough work or "too hard" caps it
A project is a good STRETCH when most of its techniques are known and one or two are new, just above the level."""
import time

from . import techniques as tq
from .db.database import DB

PRIOR_LEVEL = {0: 0.6, 1: 1.6, 2: 2.6, 3: 3.6}   # self-report 0-3 -> level
PRIOR_CONF = 0.2
KNOWN_GAP, NEW_GAP = 0.3, 1.5                      # level within 0.3 of the tier = known; up to 1.5 below = new


def _stats(db: DB, tid: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    r = db.conn.execute("SELECT hard,easy FROM technique_stats WHERE technique_id=?", (tid,)).fetchone()
    return (r["hard"], r["easy"]) if r else (0, 0)


def tier(db: DB, tid: str) -> float:
    return tq.effective_tier(tid, *_stats(db, tid))


def estimate(db: DB, maker_id: int, tid: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
    r = db.conn.execute("SELECT level,confidence FROM skill_estimates WHERE maker_id=? AND technique_id=?", (maker_id, tid)).fetchone()
    if r:
        return r["level"], r["confidence"]
    self_report = db.skills(maker_id).get(tq.craft_id())
    return PRIOR_LEVEL.get(self_report, PRIOR_LEVEL[1]), PRIOR_CONF


def _save(db: DB, maker_id: int, tid: str, level: float, conf: float) -> None:
    db.conn.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO skill_estimates VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)",
                    (maker_id, tid, max(0.0, min(5.0, level)), max(0.0, min(1.0, conf)), time.time()))
    db.conn.commit()


def _move(db: DB, maker_id: int, tid: str, target: float, weight: float, *, lower: bool = False) -> dict | None:
    """Move the level toward `target` by `weight`. Success only raises; `lower=True` allows lowering (rough work, too hard)."""
    level, conf = estimate(db, maker_id, tid)
    new = level + (target - level) * weight
    if not lower:
        new = max(level, new)
    new_conf = conf + (1 - conf) * min(1.0, weight * 0.8)
    _save(db, maker_id, tid, new, new_conf)
    if abs(new - level) < 0.05 and abs(new_conf - conf) < 0.02:
        return None
    return {"technique": tid, "name": tq.get(tid)["name"], "from": round(level, 1), "to": round(new, 1)}


# ---- evidence ----
def apply_completion(db: DB, maker_id: int, idea: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Finished a project: its techniques were doable. Raises levels a little, confidence more."""
    return [c for t in tq.for_idea(idea) if (c := _move(db, maker_id, t, tier(db, t) + 0.4, 0.25))]


def apply_photo(db: DB, maker_id: int, analysis: dict) -> list[dict]:

"""Skill model with synthetic personas: beginner, intermediate, advanced. Direction of change is what matters."""
import pytest

from app import skill, techniques as tq
from app.db.database import DB

GIFT_BOX = {"id": "origami-gift-box", "craft_id": "origami"}                 # valley, precrease, tuck (tiers 1,1,2)
CRANE = {"id": "origami-crane-garland", "craft_id": "origami"}               # + inside reverse (2), bird base (3)


def maker(self_report=None):
    d = DB(":memory:")
    mid = d.insert("makers", name="M", age_group="adult", available_time=120, restricted_tools=[])
    if self_report is not None:
        d.replace_skills(mid, {"origami": self_report})
    return d, mid


def test_taxonomy_is_consistent():
    t = tq.all_techniques()
    assert 20 <= len(t) <= 40 and all(1 <= x["tier"] <= 5 for x in t.values())
    for x in t.values():
        for p in x["prereqs"]:
            assert p in t and t[p]["tier"] <= x["tier"], (x["id"], p)
    for rid, techs in tq._data()["recipes"].items():
        assert techs and all(i in t for i in techs), rid
    for form, rules in tq._data()["pair_rules"].items():
        assert all(i in t for lvl in rules.values() for i in lvl)


def test_ideas_map_to_techniques_only_inside_the_taxonomy_craft():
    assert tq.for_idea(GIFT_BOX) == ["valley-fold", "precrease", "lock-and-tuck"]
    assert tq.for_idea({"id": "x", "craft_id": "air-dry-clay"}) == []
    pair = {"id": "pair-origami-penguin", "craft_id": "origami", "tier": 2, "motif_form": "figure", "complexity": 0}
    detailed = {**pair, "complexity": 2}

"""Reading a photo of something the maker made (or is making).

Gemini only OBSERVES: the craft, finished vs work-in-progress, which taxonomy techniques are visible and how well they
were done, tools and materials seen, and how sure it is. Code validates every field (unknown techniques dropped, numbers
clamped), caches the result per photo so it is never analysed twice, and does all skill maths in skill.py. Low
confidence never moves a skill: it produces a question for the maker instead."""
import json
import time
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator

from . import importer, skill, techniques as tq
from .agent.gemini import QuotaGuard, explain, make_model
from .core.text import norm, owns
from .db.database import DB

ASK = "I'm not sure what I'm looking at. Did you make this yourself, or follow a kit?"


class SeenTechnique(BaseModel):
    id: str
    quality: float = Field(0.5, description="0 = visibly rough, 1 = clean and well executed")
    confidence: float = Field(0.5, description="how sure you are that this technique is visible")


class PhotoAnalysis(BaseModel):
    craft: str = Field("", description="the craft, e.g. origami, knitting, painting")
    stage: Literal["finished", "wip", "unclear"] = "unclear"
    techniques: list[SeenTechnique] = Field(default_factory=list)
    quality_signals: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="evenness, symmetry, finishing: 0 to 1")
    tools_seen: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    materials_seen: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    overall_confidence: float = 0.5

    @field_validator("tools_seen", "materials_seen", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _names(cls, v): return [" ".join(str(x).split())[:40] for x in (v or [])][:10]


def instructions() -> str:
    lines = "\n".join(f"- {t['id']}: {t['name']}, {t['hint']}" for t in tq.all_techniques().values())
    return f"""You look at ONE photo of a handmade craft and report what is visible. You only observe; you never advise.
- craft: what craft it is. stage: finished, wip (work in progress) or unclear.
- techniques: ONLY ids from this list, only those you can actually see evidence of, each with quality (0 rough to 1 clean) and your confidence:
{lines}
- quality_signals: evenness, symmetry, finishing, each 0 to 1.
- tools_seen and materials_seen: plain names of things visible in the photo.
- overall_confidence: 0 to 1. If the photo is blurry, shows no craft, or you are guessing, give a LOW number. Do not guess."""


def clean(raw: PhotoAnalysis) -> dict:
    """Everything the model said is untrusted until here."""
    clamp = lambda x: max(0.0, min(1.0, float(x)))
    seen: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for t in raw.techniques:
        if t.id in tq.all_techniques() and t.id not in seen:
            seen[t.id] = {"id": t.id, "quality": clamp(t.quality), "confidence": clamp(t.confidence)}
    craft = " ".join(raw.craft.lower().split())[:40]
    in_taxonomy = tq.craft_id() in craft or "paper fold" in craft
    return {"craft": craft, "stage": raw.stage, "overall_confidence": clamp(raw.overall_confidence),
            "techniques": list(seen.values())[:8] if in_taxonomy else [],
            "quality_signals": {k: clamp(v) for k, v in list(raw.quality_signals.items())[:4]},
            "tools_seen": raw.tools_seen, "materials_seen": raw.materials_seen}


def _inventory_suggestions(db: DB, a: dict) -> dict:
    mats = [m["name"] for m in db.all("materials")]
    tools = [t["name"] for t in db.all("tools")]
    return {"materials": [m for m in a["materials_seen"] if not owns(m, mats)][:6],
            "tools": [t for t in a["tools_seen"] if not owns(t, tools)][:6]}

"""Finishing a project: difficulty report, 'what was hard?', recalibration, completion stats, and stretch ranking."""
import pytest

from app import pipeline, plans, skill
from app.core.models import Request
from tests.test_two_tier import PAPER, mk


def plan(d, idea, rid=1, mid=1):
    return plans.create(d, recipient_id=rid, maker_id=mid, idea_id=idea, occasion="diwali")


def test_too_hard_asks_what_was_hard_and_changes_nothing_until_answered():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    p = plan(d, "origami-crane-garland")
    before = skill.profile(d, 1)
    out = plans.finish_detailed(d, p, rating=3, difficulty="too_hard")
    ask = out["ask_hard"]
    assert ask and ask["free_text"] and {"bird-base", "inside-reverse-fold"} <= {t["id"] for t in ask["techniques"]}
    assert all(t["name"] for t in ask["techniques"])
    hard_levels = {r["id"]: r["level"] for r in skill.profile(d, 1) if r["id"] in ("bird-base", "inside-reverse-fold")}
    # completion alone may nudge levels up, but nothing was lowered yet
    assert all(hard_levels[t["id"]] >= {r["id"]: r["level"] for r in before}[t["id"]] for t in ask["techniques"] if t["id"] in hard_levels)
    changes = plans.answer_hard(d, out["gift_id"], ["bird-base"], "the last fold")
    assert [c["technique"] for c in changes] == ["bird-base"] and changes[0]["to"] < changes[0]["from"]
    with pytest.raises(plans.PlanError):
        plans.answer_hard(d, out["gift_id"], ["bird-base"])                 # answered once
    row = d.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM difficulty_feedback WHERE gift_id=?", (out["gift_id"],)).fetchone()
    assert row["note"] == "the last fold" and "bird-base" in row["hard_techniques"]


def test_too_easy_and_right_are_applied_straight_away_and_unknown_techniques_ignored():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    out = plans.finish_detailed(d, plan(d, "origami-gift-box"), rating=5, difficulty="too_easy")
    assert out["ask_hard"] is None and out["changes"]
    d2 = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    p = plan(d2, "origami-gift-box")
    out = plans.finish_detailed(d2, p, rating=3, difficulty="too_hard")
    assert plans.answer_hard(d2, out["gift_id"], ["not-a-technique"]) is not None   # falls back to a gentle all-techniques change


def test_a_craft_without_techniques_still_asks_in_words():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    out = plans.finish_detailed(d, plan(d, "coupon-book"), rating=3, difficulty="too_hard")
    assert out["ask_hard"] == {"gift_id": out["gift_id"], "free_text": True, "techniques": []}


def test_area_level_grows_with_finished_projects():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    d.replace_skills(1, {"origami": 0})
    grown = None
    for _ in range(3):
        out = plans.finish_detailed(d, plan(d, "origami-gift-box"), rating=4)
        grown = out["level_up"] or grown
    assert grown and grown["to"] >= 2 and d.skills(1)["origami"] >= 2


def test_stats_report_completion_and_difficulty_rates():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    plan(d, "origami-gift-box")
    plans.finish_detailed(d, plan(d, "origami-gift-box"), rating=4, difficulty="right")
    s = plans.stats(d)
    assert s["planned"] == 2 and s["completed"] == 1 and s["completion_rate"] == 0.5 and s["right_difficulty_rate"] == 1.0

        return r["suggestions"]
    beginner, expert = top(0), top(3)
    assert [s.idea_id for s in beginner] != [s.idea_id for s in expert]
    assert any(s.learn for s in beginner + expert)                       # ideas say what they would teach
    assert all(len(s.learn) <= 2 for s in beginner)                      # beginners are not handed three new techniques at once

        from datetime import date as D

            for year in (t.year, t.year + 1):
                try:
                    nxt = d.replace(year=year)
                except ValueError:  # 29 Feb
                    nxt = D(year, 3, 1)
                if nxt >= t:
                    break
            try:
                self.conn.execute("UPDATE occasions SET date=?, status='upcoming' WHERE id=?", (nxt.isoformat(), r["id"]))

class ProfileError(ValueError):
    """A problem the user can fix; the message is shown as-is."""


def _strength(score: float) -> int:

from datetime import date, timedelta

import pytest

from app import plans, profiles, skill
from tests.test_two_tier import PAPER, mk


def test_taste_is_learned_shown_and_correctable():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"])
    d.bump_pref(1, "Tulips", 4.5)
    d.bump_pref(1, "glitter", -2.5)
    d.bump_pref(1, "noise", 0.1)                       # too weak to show
    p = profiles.recipient_profile(d, 1)
    assert [t["tag"] for t in p["loved"]] == ["Tulips"] and p["loved"][0]["strength"] == 3
    assert [t["tag"] for t in p["disliked"]] == ["glitter"] and p["disliked"][0]["strength"] == 2
    profiles.taste_action(d, 1, "glitter", "forget")
    assert profiles.recipient_profile(d, 1)["disliked"] == []
    profiles.taste_action(d, 1, "Tulips", "like")      # pin: becomes an explicit like, no longer a guess
    r = d.get("recipients", 1)
    assert "Tulips" in r["likes"] and profiles.recipient_profile(d, 1)["loved"] == []
    profiles.taste_action(d, 1, "tulips", "dislike")   # changing your mind moves it across
    r = d.get("recipients", 1)
    assert "tulips" in r["dislikes"] and "Tulips" not in r["likes"]
    with pytest.raises(profiles.ProfileError):
        profiles.taste_action(d, 1, "x", "explode")


def test_a_persons_date_is_yearly_and_rolls_forward():
    d = mk(PAPER)
    today = date.today()
    past = today - timedelta(days=10)
    oid = profiles.add_date(d, 1, "Birthday", past.replace(year=past.year - 20).isoformat())   # born long ago
    row = d.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM occasions WHERE id=?", (oid,)).fetchone()
    nxt = date.fromisoformat(row["date"])
    assert nxt >= today and nxt.year in (today.year, today.year + 1) and row["repeat"] == "yearly" and row["recipient_id"] == 1
    d.conn.execute("UPDATE occasions SET status='dismissed' WHERE id=?", (oid,))              # done this year...
    d.conn.execute("UPDATE occasions SET date=? WHERE id=?", ((today - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat(), oid))
    up = [o for o in d.upcoming_occasions(today.isoformat()) if o["id"] == oid]
    assert up and up[0]["status"] == "upcoming" and up[0]["date"] >= today.isoformat()        # ...comes back next year
    assert profiles.recipient_profile(d, 1)["dates"

Items 1 to 4 are built, and I did not build Telegram. All 145 tests pass (25 new), and the server is running at http://localhost:8765. I tested the photo reading live on Gemini and checked the new pages in screenshots. I haven't clicked through the "what was hard?" follow-up in a real browser.

Why not Telegram: the web app already covers everything on a phone, including the camera. The only gain was push reminders, so I skipped it.

What was added - Technique taxonomy (origami). There are 22 techniques with a tier from 1 to 5 and prerequisites. The 10 fixed origami recipes are linked to techniques explicitly. The craft-and-subject ideas get techniques from the kind of subject and how detailed it is. - Skill model. Each maker has a level and a confidence for every technique, and all the maths is plain code. - Starting point. It starts from the maker's own 0–3 rating, with low confidence. - Raising. Finishing a project raises levels a little. A good photo raises them more, and a work-in-progress photo counts for more. - Lowering. A visibly rough photo caps a level. "Too hard" only ever lowers it. - Calibration. Enough "too hard" or "too easy" reports slowly move a technique's tier. - Other crafts. Crafts outside origami get a simple level that rises as you finish projects (3 finished lifts you to level 2, 6 to level 3). - Photo analysis. - Upload. The home page upload has a "read it for [maker]" choice. Gemini reports the craft, whether it's finished or in progress, the techniques it sees and how well they were done, and the tools and materials visible. - Checks and caching. Code drops unknown techniques and clamps the numbers. Each photo is read once and never re-analysed. - Unsure photos. If Gemini is unsure, it asks "did you make this yourself or follow a kit?" and changes no skills. - Basket suggestions. The tools and materials it sees are offered with a "+" button to add to your basket. - Feedback loop. Finishing a plan now asks "just right / too easy / too hard". - If it was hard: the app asks which techniques were hard, from that project's own list, plus a free-text box and a Skip button. Only the techniques you name are lowered. If you skip, it lowers all of them gently. - Completion stats: completion rate and "felt just right" rate show on the maker page. - Stretch ranking. Ideas that use techniques now score higher when most are known and one or two are new. They score lower when nothing is new, or when there is a big jump. When your level is a guess, the safer pick wins. Cards say "You'd learn: …". - Profile pages. - Person page: it shows the taste the app learned from your ratings, and you can keep it as a real like or dislike, or forget it. It also lists yearly dates and gift history. Dates such as a birthday come back by themselves each year. - Maker page: it shows a skill meter per technique, calibration questions, good next steps, and the things they've made. Guesses are drawn faint and labelled "probably fine". - Profiles list: names now open these pages, and a pencil icon edits. - Agent. It can read skills and ask the calibration questions.

Limits - The taxonomy covers origami only, because that's the craft I built the technique list for. Other crafts use the simple per-craft level. - Technique links for the craft-and-subject ideas come from a rule, so they are approximate. The fixed recipes' links are my own and aren't checked by a crafter. - Photo reading is the shakiest part, because Gemini's guesses about craftsmanship are noisy. That's why low confidence never moves a skill. I only tested it on a crude drawing, which it correctly rejected, so I haven't seen it on a real origami photo. - All of this uses your free quota: about 1 request per photo and 2 to 3 per chat message. 124 of 150 are left today.

are we done with the agent
Claude's response

Mostly yes. The agent works end to end and the tests pass, but a few things are still open.

Done (plan.md phases 0–6 and 8) - Setup: the Gemini key is read from .env, and it uses gemini-3.5-flash-lite on the free tier. - Data and skills: the origami technique list and the skill model with confidence are in. - Photos: photo analysis is in, and it asks a question when it's unsure. - Ideas: research uses DuckDuckGo search, because Google Search grounding returns 429 on your free key. - Ranking: stretch-based ranking is in. - Planner: the planner chat has 15 tools. It can only show ideas that came from its own lookups, and it falls back to the rule-based path when Gemini is unusable. - Feedback: the "too easy / just right / too hard" loop is in, and "too hard" asks which technique was hard. - Interface: the web app replaces the Telegram step, since you ruled Telegram out.

Not done or not proven - Real use: I haven't clicked through the app in a real browser. I also haven't run photo analysis on an actual origami photo, only on a crude drawing. - Crafts: only origami has a technique list. Other crafts use a simple per-craft level. - Photo privacy: I haven't added a delete option for photos of other people, which plan.md lists under the interface phase. - Regression set: I haven't built the saved set of photos and personas to re-run when prompts or models change. - Agent weaknesses: flash-lite is weaker at calling tools than the full flash models, and the free quota is 150 requests a day. - Research: online ideas are rewritten from search snippets, so their steps are vague.

The most useful next step is for you to use it for a day: add a real maker, upload a real photo, and finish one plan. That would show whether the skill levels and the "what was hard?" flow behave sensibly. Do you want me to build the photo delete option first, or leave everything until you've tried it?

"""Photos of things the user has made, shown together on the home page.

Two sources, merged newest first: photos added straight to the gallery ("I made this"), and the photo of a
finished gift from a plan. Uploads go through the same re-encoding as every other image (EXIF/GPS dropped)."""
import time

from . import importer
from .db.database import DB


class GalleryError(ValueError):
    """A problem the user can fix; the message is shown as-is."""


def add(db: DB, photo: bytes, *, title: str = "", note: str = "", idea_id: str = "") -> int:
    if not photo:
        raise GalleryError("Choose or take a photo first.")
    try:
        name = importer.store(importer.sanitise(photo)[0])
    except importer.InputError as e:
        raise GalleryError(str(e))
    cur = db.conn.execute("INSERT INTO creations(title,note,photo,idea_id,created) VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)",
                          (title.strip()[:80], note.strip()[:300], name, idea_id[:80], time.time()))
    db.conn.commit()
    return cur.lastrowid


def items(db: DB, limit: int = 60) -> list[dict]:
    made = [{"kind": "made", "id": r["id"], "title": r["title"], "note": r["note"], "photo": r["photo"],
             "created": r["created"], "for": ""} for r in db.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM creations")]
    gifts = [{"kind": "gift", "id": r["id"], "title": r["title"] or "A gift", "note": r["note"], "photo": r["photo"],
              "created": r["date"], "for": r["name"] or ""}
             for r in db.conn.execute("SELECT g.id,g.note,g.photo,g.date,r.name,g.idea_id,"
                                      "(SELECT json_extract(data,'$.title') FROM ideas WHERE id=g.idea_id) AS title "
                                      "FROM gifts g LEFT JOIN recipients r ON r.id=g.recipient_id WHERE g.photo!=''")]
    return sorted(made + gifts, key=lambda x: -x["created"])[:limit]


def delete(db: DB, creation_id: int) -> bool:
    row = db.conn.execute("SELECT photo FROM creations WHERE id=?", (creation_id,)).fetchone()
    if not row:
        return False
    db.conn.execute("DELETE FROM creations WHERE id=?", (creation_id,))
    db.conn.commit()
    importer.delete_images([row["photo"]])
    return True
    return {"ready": g.usable(), "model": config.AGENT_MODEL, "left_today": g.left_today(), "per_day": g.per_day}


# ---- gallery: photos of things the user made ------------------------------------
@router.post("/gallery", status_code=201)
async def add_creation(r: HttpRequest, photo: UploadFile = File(...), title: str = Form(""), note: str = Form(""),
                       idea_id: str = Form(""), maker_id: int | None = Form(None)):
    raw = await photo.read()
    try:
        cid = gallery.add(db(r), raw, title=title, note=note, idea_id=idea_id)
    except gallery.GalleryError as e:
        raise HTTPException(422, str(e))
    out = {"id": cid, "reading": None}
    if maker_id and db(r).get("makers", maker_id):   # read it: techniques seen, skill updates, a question if unsure
        name = db(r).conn.execute("SELECT photo FROM creations WHERE id=?", (cid,)).fetchone()["photo"]
        out["reading"] = await run_in_threadpool(photo_analysis.analyze, db(r), r.app.state.guard, maker_id, name, raw)
    return out


@router.get("/gallery")
def list_gallery(r: HttpRequest):
    return gallery.items(db(r))


@router.delete("/gallery/{creation_id}", status_code=204)
def delete_creation(creation_id: int, r: HttpRequest):
    if not gallery.delete(db(r), creation_id):
        raise HTTPException(404, "not found")

import io

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from PIL import Image

from app import gallery, plans
from app.db.database import DB


def jpg(color="red"):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    Image.new("RGB", (40, 30), color).save(buf, "JPEG")
    return buf.getvalue()


def test_add_list_delete_and_bad_upload(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from app import config
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "PHOTOS_DIR", tmp_path)
    d = DB(":memory:")
    cid = gallery.add(d, jpg(), title="Paper star", note="for Maa")
    items = gallery.items(d)
    assert [i["title"] for i in items] == ["Paper star"] and items[0]["kind"] == "made"
    assert (tmp_path / "ideas" / items[0]["photo"]).exists()
    for bad in (b"", b"not an image"):
        try:
            gallery.add(d, bad)
            assert False
        except gallery.GalleryError:
            pass
    assert gallery.delete(d, cid) and not gallery.delete(d, cid) and gallery.items(d) == []
    assert not (tmp_path / "ideas" / items[0]["photo"]).exists()


def test_finished_gift_photos_appear_with_the_recipient(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from app import config
    from tests.test_two_tier import PAPER, mk
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "PHOTOS_DIR", tmp_path)
    d = mk(PAPER)
    pid = plans.create(d, recipient_id=1, maker_id=1, idea_id="origami-lotus-diya", occasion="diwali")
    plans.finish(d, pid, rating=5, note="she loved it", photo=jpg("blue"))
    gallery.add(d, jpg(), title="Mine")
    items = gallery.items(d)
    assert {i["kind"] for i in items} == {"made", "gift"}
    gift = next(i for i in items if i["kind"] == "gift")
    assert gift["for"] == "R" and gift["title"]

"""Skill model with synthetic personas: beginner, intermediate, advanced. Direction of change is what matters."""
import pytest

from app import skill, techniques as tq
from app.db.database import DB

GIFT_BOX = {"id": "origami-gift-box", "craft_id": "origami"}                 # valley, precrease, tuck (tiers 1,1,2)
CRANE = {"id": "origami-crane-garland", "craft_id": "origami"}               # + inside reverse (2), bird base (3)


def maker(self_report=None):
    d = DB(":memory:")
    mid = d.insert("makers", name="M", age_group="adult", available_time=120, restricted_tools=[])
    if self_report is not None:
        d.replace_skills(mid, {"origami": self_report})
    return d, mid


def test_taxonomy_is_consistent():
    t = tq.all_techniques()
    assert 20 <= len(t) <= 40 and all(1 <= x["tier"] <= 5 for x in t.values())
    for x in t.values():
        for p in x["prereqs"]:
            assert p in t and t[p]["tier"] <= x["tier"], (x["id"], p)
    for rid, techs in tq._data()["recipes"].items():
        assert techs and all(i in t for i in techs), rid
    for form, rules in tq._data()["pair_rules"].items():
        assert all(i in t for lvl in rules.values() for i in lvl)


def test_ideas_map_to_techniques_only_inside_the_taxonomy_craft():
    assert tq.for_idea(GIFT_BOX) == ["valley-fold", "precrease", "lock-and-tuck"]
    assert tq.for_idea({"id": "x", "craft_id": "air-dry-clay"}) == []
    pair = {"id": "pair-origami-penguin", "craft_id": "origami", "tier": 2, "motif_form": "figure", "complexity": 0}
    detailed = {**pair, "complexity": 2}
    assert set(tq.for_idea(pair)) < set(tq.for_idea(detailed))


def test_prior_comes_from_self_report_with_low_confidence():
    d, m = maker(0)
    lvl, conf = skill.estimate(d, m, "valley-fold")
    assert lvl < 1 and conf < 0.3
    d2, m2 = maker(3)
    assert skill.estimate(d2, m2, "valley-fold")[0] > 3


def test_finishing_projects_raises_levels_and_confidence_but_never_lowers():
    d, m = maker(0)
    before = {t: skill.estimate(d, m, t) for t in tq.for_idea(CRANE)}
    skill.apply_completion(d, m, CRANE)
    for t, (l0, c0) in before.items():
        l1, c1 = skill.estimate(d, m, t)
        assert l1 >= l0 and c1 > c0
    d3, m3 = maker(3)

# ---- evidence ----
def apply_completion(db: DB, maker_id: int, idea: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Finished a project: its techniques were doable. Raises levels a little, confidence more."""
    return [c for t in tq.for_idea(idea) if (c := _move(db, maker_id, t, tier(db, t) + 0.4, 0.25))]


def apply_photo(db: DB, maker_id: int, analysis: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """analysis: {stage, overall_confidence, techniques:[{id, quality, confidence}]} (already validated)."""
    if analysis.get("overall_confidence", 0) < 0.4:
        return []  # too unsure: ask the maker instead of guessing
    wip = analysis.get("stage") == "wip"
    out = []
    for o in analysis.get("techniques", []):
        tid, q, c = o["id"], o["quality"], o["confidence"] * analysis["overall_confidence"]
        if q >= 0.7:
            ch = _move(db, maker_id, tid, tier(db, tid) + 0.6, 0.35 * c * (1.5 if wip else 1.0))
        elif q < 0.4:  # visibly rough: cap at the technique's tier
            level, conf = estimate(db, maker_id, tid)
            capped = min(level, tier(db, tid))
            _save(db, maker_id, tid, capped, conf + (1 - conf) * 0.4 * c)
            ch = {"technique": tid, "name": tq.get(tid)["name"], "from": round(level, 1), "to": round(capped, 1)} if capped < level - 0.05 else None
        else:
            ch = _move(db, maker_id, tid, tier(db, tid), 0.1 * c)
        if ch:
            out.append(ch)
    return out


def apply_difficulty(db: DB, maker_id: int, idea: dict, difficulty: str, hard: list[str] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """difficulty: too_easy | right | too_hard. For too_hard, `hard` names the techniques that were hard."""
    techs = tq.for_idea(idea)
    out = []
    if difficulty == "too_hard":
        blamed = [t for t in (hard or []) if t in techs] or techs  # nothing named: all of them, more gently
        for t in blamed:
            level = estimate(db, maker_id, t)[0]
            out += [c for c in [_move(db, maker_id, t, min(tier(db, t) - 0.8, level - 0.4), 0.5 if hard else 0.25, lower=True)] if c]
            _vote(db, t, hard=1)
    elif difficulty == "too_easy":
        for t in techs:
            out += [c for c in [_move(db, maker_id, t, tier(db, t) + 0.9, 0.3)] if c]
            _vote(db, t, easy=1)
    else:  # right: the estimate was about right, so we are more sure of it
        for t in techs:
            level, conf = estimate(db, maker_id, t)
            _save(db, maker_id, t, level, conf + (1 - conf) * 0.15)
    return out

    id: str
    quality: float = Field(0.5, description="0 = visibly rough, 1 = clean and well executed")
    confidence: float = Field(0.5, description="how sure you are that this technique is visible")

    materials_seen: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    overall_confidence: float = 0.5

    @field_validator("tools_seen", "materials_seen", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _names(cls, v): return [" ".join(str(x).split())[:40] for x in (v or [])][:10]
