"""Regression set: synthetic makers and photo-reader outputs, kept as data in tests/regression/.
Add a case there when a bug is found. Real photos are checked live with scripts/regress_photos.py."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from app import photo_analysis, skill, techniques as tq
from app.agent.gemini import QuotaGuard
from app.db.database import DB
from tests.test_skill import jpeg, maker, vision
from tests.test_two_tier import PAPER, mk, run

HERE = Path(__file__).parent / "regression"
PERSONAS = json.loads((HERE / "personas.json").read_text())
PHOTO_CASES = json.loads((HERE / "photo_cases.json").read_text())["cases"]


def levels(d, m, techs):
    return {t: skill.estimate(d, m, t)[0] for t in techs}


def check(direction, before, after, tid, where):
    if direction == "up":
        assert after > before + 0.01, f"{where}: {tid} should rise ({before:.2f} -> {after:.2f})"
    elif direction == "down":
        assert after < before - 0.01, f"{where}: {tid} should fall ({before:.2f} -> {after:.2f})"
    elif direction == "same":
        assert abs(after - before) < 0.01, f"{where}: {tid} should not move ({before:.2f} -> {after:.2f})"
    elif direction == "capped":
        assert after <= tq.get(tid)["tier"] + 0.01, f"{where}: {tid} should be capped at its tier ({after:.2f})"
    else:
        raise AssertionError(f"unknown direction {direction}")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("persona", PERSONAS["personas"], ids=lambda p: p["name"])
def test_persona_event_sequence_moves_skills_as_expected(persona):
    d, m = maker(persona["self_report"])
    ideas = PERSONAS["ideas"]
    for i, ev in enumerate(persona["events"]):
        where = f"{persona['name']} / event {i + 1} ({ev['do']})"
        watch = set(ev["expect"]) | set(tq.for_idea(ideas[ev["idea"]]) if "idea" in ev else [])
        before = levels(d, m, watch)
        if ev["do"] == "complete":
            skill.apply_completion(d, m, ideas[ev["idea"]])
        elif ev["do"] == "photo":
            skill.apply_photo(d, m, ev["analysis"])
        elif ev["do"] == "difficulty":
            skill.apply_difficulty(d, m, ideas[ev["idea"]], ev["difficulty"], ev.get("hard"))
        else:
            raise AssertionError(f"unknown event {ev['do']}")
        after = levels(d, m, watch)
        for tid, direction in ev["expect"].items():
            check(direction, before[tid], after[tid], tid, where)
        assert all(0 <= v <= 5 for v in after.values()), f"{where}: level out of range"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", PHOTO_CASES, ids=lambda c: c["name"])
def test_photo_reader_handles_each_kind_of_model_output(case):
    d, m = maker(case["start_level"])
    calls = []
    out = photo_analysis.analyze(d, QuotaGuard(d), m, "x.jpg", jpeg(), model=vision(case["raw"], calls))
    exp = case["expect"]
    assert out["error"] is None
    assert [t["id"] for t in out["analysis"]["techniques"]] == exp["techniques"]
    assert bool(out["question"]) == exp["question"]
    assert bool(out["changes"]) == exp["changes"]
    if exp.get("all_in_0_1"):
        a = out["analysis"]
        assert 0 <= a["overall_confidence"] <= 1 and all(0 <= t["quality"] <= 1 and 0 <= t["confidence"] <= 1 for t in a["techniques"])
    again = photo_analysis.analyze(d, QuotaGuard(d), m, "x.jpg", jpeg(), model=vision(case["raw"], calls))
    assert again["cached"] and len(calls) == 1          # a photo is read once, never again

Bash: cat > scripts/regress_photos.py <<'E' """Live check of the photo reader against photos YOU labelled 
cat > scripts/regress_photos.py <<'E'
"""Live check of the photo reader against photos YOU labelled (see tests/regression/photos/README.md).
Uses about 1 free Gemini request per photo. Reads and writes nothing in the real app data except the daily request counter.
   env -u PYTHONPATH uv run python scripts/regress_photos.py"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
from app import photo_analysis  # noqa: E402
from app.agent.gemini import QuotaGuard  # noqa: E402
from app.db.database import DB  # noqa: E402

FOLDER = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "tests" / "regression" / "photos"


def judge(label: dict, a: dict) -> list[str]:
    """-> list of problems (empty = pass)."""
    bad = []
    if label.get("craft") and label["craft"].lower() not in a["craft"]:
        bad.append(f"craft: said '{a['craft']}', expected '{label['craft']}'")
    unsure = a["overall_confidence"] < 0.5 or a["stage"] == "unclear"
    if label.get("ambiguous"):
        if not unsure:
            bad.append("should have been unsure about an ambiguous photo")
        return bad
    if unsure:
        bad.append(f"unsure (confidence {a['overall_confidence']:.2f}, stage {a['stage']}) about a clear photo")
    if label.get("stage") and a["stage"] not in (label["stage"], "unclear"):
        bad.append(f"stage: said {a['stage']}, expected {label['stage']}")
    invented = [t["id"] for t in a["techniques"] if t["id"] not in label.get("techniques", [])]
    if invented:
        bad.append(f"reported techniques that are not in the photo: {invented}")
    if a["techniques"] and label.get("quality") in ("clean", "rough"):
        q = sum(t["quality"] for t in a["techniques"]) / len(a["techniques"])
        if label["quality"] == "clean" and q < 0.6 or label["quality"] == "rough" and q > 0.45:
            bad.append(f"quality: labelled {label['quality']}, reader gave {q:.2f}")
    return bad


def main() -> int:
    labels_file = FOLDER / "labels.json"
    if not labels_file.exists():
        print(f"No labels yet. Add photos and {labels_file.name} in {FOLDER} (see README.md there).")
        return 2
    labels = json.loads(labels_file.read_text())
    guard = QuotaGuard(DB())                       # real counter, so the free daily budget is respected
    scratch = DB(":memory:")
    mid = scratch.insert("makers", name="regression", age_group="adult", available_time=60, restricted_tools=[])
    failed, report = 0, []
    for lab in labels:
        path = FOLDER / lab["file"]
        if not path.exists():
            print(f"MISSING  {lab['file']}")
            failed += 1
            continue
        out = photo_analysis.analyze(scratch, guard, mid, lab["file"], path.read_bytes())
        if out["error"]:
            print(f"ERROR    {lab['file']}: {out['error']}")
            failed += 1
            continue
        problems = judge(lab, out["analysis"])
        failed += bool(problems)
        print(("FAIL     " if problems else "ok       ") + lab["file"] + "".join(f"\n           - {p}" for p in problems))
        report.append({"file": lab["file"], "problems": problems, "analysis": out["analysis"]})
    (FOLDER / "last_report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=1))
    print(f"\n{len(labels) - failed}/{len(labels)} passed. Details: tests/regression/photos/last_report.json. Free requests left today: {guard.left_today()}")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Research agent: finds real, sourced ideas for ONE craft on the web, for ONE maker.

A small pydantic-ai agent (Gemini + its built-in web search, one structured answer, at most a few model requests).
What it may see: the craft, the occasion, the maker's age group / skill level / restricted tools, what materials
the maker owns, and titles it should not repeat. It never sees names, allergies, photos or the calendar.
What it may NOT decide: safety. Whatever it returns is rewritten into our schema and then passes the same code
checks as every other idea (safety flags derived from the text, age, restricted tools, prices, duplicates, denied
words). Anything that fails is dropped, and what survives is stored as an unverified "found online" idea with its
source link, removable with one click."""
import hashlib
import re
import time
from typing import Literal
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator

from . import config, importer, pairing
from .core import filters
from .core.text import norm
from .db.database import DB
from .motif_discovery import CRAFT_WORDS, DENY, near_duplicate

MAX_IDEAS = 3
MAX_REQUESTS = 6  # model round trips (search + answer) per run
_FIELD = lambda v, n: " ".join(str(v).split())[:n]


class FoundIdea(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str = ""
    materials: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    steps: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    difficulty: Literal["easy", "medium", "hard"] = "medium"
    time_minutes: int = 60
    tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    source_url: str = ""

    @field_validator("title", "description", "source_url", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _clip(cls, v): return _FIELD(v or "", 300)

    @field_validator("materials", "tools", "tags", "steps", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _list(cls, v): return [_FIELD(x, 200) for x in (v or [])][:14]


class Found(BaseModel):
    ideas: list[FoundIdea] = Field(default_factory=list)


class ResearchError(Exception):
    """Something the user can act on; the message is shown as-is."""


def enabled() -> bool:
    return bool(config.GEMINI_API_KEY)


def instructions(age_group: str, restricted: list[str]) -> str:
    blocked = ", ".join(sorted(filters.AGE_BLOCKED.get(age_group, set())) ) or "nothing in particular"
    return f"""You find real handmade-gift project ideas on the web for ONE craft and return them as JSON.
Use web search to find well-regarded tutorials, then describe each project IN YOUR OWN WORDS (never copy text).
Rules:
- The maker's age group is "{age_group}". Do not suggest anything involving: {blocked}. Prefer simple, low-risk methods.
- Never require these tools: {', '.join(restricted) or 'none restricted'}.
- Every idea must be a gift someone could make at home in the given time, from common craft materials.
- Use the materials the maker already owns where you can. Name materials and tools plainly (e.g. "colored paper", "scissors").
- 4 to 8 short steps per idea. Mention any hazard (heat, sharp blade, small parts) in the step where it happens.
- source_url must be the https page you actually used. Skip ideas you cannot source.
- Do not repeat any title in avoid_titles. Return at most {MAX_IDEAS} ideas.
Reply with JSON only: {{"ideas":[{{"title":"","description":"","materials":[],"tools":[],"steps":[],"difficulty":"easy|medium|hard","time_minutes":45,"tags":[],"source_url":"https://"}}]}}"""

ask for rule-checked suggestions but can never change a rule: safety, age, allergies, budget, restricted tools,
prices and duplicates are all enforced in code. Results are kept small because free-tier tokens are limited."""

@dataclass
class Deps:
    db: DB
    recipient_id: int | None = None
    maker_id: int | None = None
    occasion: str = ""
    cards: dict = field(default_factory=dict)      # idea_id -> Suggestion, filled by suggest_ideas (shown to the user)
    actions: list = field(default_factory=list)    # things the agent changed, shown to the user
    searches: int = 0


class AgentReply(BaseModel):
    """What the planner finally says. Idea cards come from the suggest_ideas tool, never from the model's memory."""
    message: str = Field(description="A short, warm reply in plain language. No lists of steps.")
    idea_ids: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="idea_ids returned by suggest_ideas to show as cards (max 5)")
    questions: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="At most 2 short clarifying questions, only if really needed")


def _ids(d: Deps, recipient_id, maker_id):

# ---- the open web (free: DuckDuckGo from this machine; the page text is read by code, not by a browser) ----
def search_ideas(ctx: RunContext[Deps], query: str) -> dict:
    """Search the web for craft project ideas or tutorials. Returns up to 5 {title, url, snippet}. Use sparingly."""
    d = ctx.deps
    d.searches += 1
    if d.searches > 2:
        return {"error": "search limit for this question reached"}
    try:
        from ddgs import DDGS
        rows = DDGS().text(query[:120] + " craft DIY", max_results=5)
    except Exception:
        return {"error": "web search is unavailable right now"}
    return {"results": [{"title": r.get("title", "")[:100], "url": r.get("href", ""), "snippet": r.get("body", "")[:200]} for r in rows]}

"""Reading the open web, for free and safely: DuckDuckGo search from this machine, and page text pulled out by code.

Pages are fetched over https only, never to a private address, with no redirects followed, a size cap and a short
timeout. Only text is kept (scripts, menus and forms are dropped) and the headings, list items and paragraphs keep
their shape, because tutorials hide their real detail in numbered lists."""
import html.parser
import re
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from urllib.parse import urlparse

import httpx

from . import calendar_import

MAX_BYTES = 400_000
SKIP_HOSTS = ("youtube.", "youtu.be", "pinterest.", "facebook.", "instagram.", "tiktok.", "amazon.", "etsy.", "ebay.",
              "walmart.", "twitter.", "x.com", "reddit.", "wikipedia.")


class _Blocks(html.parser.HTMLParser):
    SKIP = {"script", "style", "nav", "footer", "header", "aside", "form", "noscript", "svg", "button", "select"}
    BLOCK = {"p": "", "li": "- ", "h1": "# ", "h2": "## ", "h3": "## ", "h4": "## ", "td": ""}

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.blocks: list[str] = []
        self.cur: list[str] = []
        self.kind = ""
        self.skip = 0

    def _flush(self):
        text = " ".join(" ".join(self.cur).split())
        if self.kind in self.BLOCK and len(text) >= 3:
            self.blocks.append(self.BLOCK[self.kind] + text)
        self.cur, self.kind = [], ""

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        self.skip += tag in self.SKIP
        if tag in self.BLOCK and not self.skip:
            self._flush()
            self.kind = tag

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag in self.BLOCK and not self.skip:
            self._flush()
        self.skip = max(0, self.skip - (tag in self.SKIP))

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if not self.skip and self.kind:
            self.cur.append(data)


def to_text(raw_html: str, limit: int = 6000) -> str:
    p = _Blocks()
    p.feed(raw_html)
    p._flush()
    seen, out, size = set(), [], 0
    for b in p.blocks:
        if b in seen or (len(b) < 20 and not b.startswith("#")):
            continue                                            # repeated menu bits and one-word fragments
        seen.add(b)
        out.append(b)
        size += len(b) + 1
        if size >= limit:
            break
    return "\n".join(out)[:limit]


def read(url: str, limit: int = 6000) -> str:
    """-> the page's text. Raises ValueError with a short reason the caller can show or ignore."""
    try:
        safe = calendar_import._public_https(url)
        with httpx.stream("GET", safe, timeout=10, follow_redirects=False, headers={"User-Agent": "GiftBulb/1.0"}) as r:
            if r.status_code != 200 or "html" not in r.headers.get("content-type", ""):
                raise ValueError(f"couldn't read that page ({r.status_code})")
            raw = b""
            for chunk in r.iter_bytes():
                raw += chunk
                if len(raw) > MAX_BYTES:
                    break
    except calendar_import.CalendarError as e:
        raise ValueError(str(e))
    except httpx.HTTPError:
        raise ValueError("couldn't download that page")
    return to_text(raw.decode("utf-8", "replace"), limit)


def search(query: str, n: int = 8) -> list[dict]:
    """-> [{title, url, snippet}], https only, minus shops, video and social sites (no readable steps there)."""
    from ddgs import DDGS
    rows = DDGS().text(query[:150], max_results=n + 6)
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        u = urlparse(r.get("href", ""))
        if u.scheme == "https" and u.hostname and not any(s in u.hostname for s in SKIP_HOSTS):
            out.append({"title": r.get("title", "")[:120], "url": r["href"], "snippet": r.get("body", "")[:200]})
    return out[:n]

def page(steps=STEPS, extra=""):
    """Page text the way webpage.to_text shapes it: headings and list items."""
    return "## How to make it\\n" + "\\n".join("- " + x for x in steps) + "\\n" + extra


def idea(title, url, **kw):
    base = {"title": title, "description": "A pretty gift.", "materials": ["colored paper"], "tools": ["scissors"],
            "steps": STEPS, "difficulty": "easy", "time_minutes": 30, "tags": ["diwali"], "source_url": url}
    return {**base, **kw}


def pages_for(*urls, **kw):
    return {u: page(**kw) for u in urls}


def fake(ideas, seen=None):
    def fn(messages, info):
        if seen is not None:
            seen.append(json.dumps([str(m) for m in messages]))
        return ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart(json.dumps({"ideas": ideas}))])
    return FunctionModel(fn)


def test_good_ideas_are_stored_labelled_and_usable():
    d = mk(PAPER, ["scissors"], maker_age="adult")
    out = research.run(d, maker_id=1, craft_id="origami", occasion="Diwali", pages=pages_for("https://example.com/diya"),
                       model=fake([idea("Folded paper diya", "https://example.com/diya")]))
    assert [a["title"] for a in out["added"]] == ["Folded paper diya"] and out["error"] is None
    stored = next(i for i in d.ideas() if i["id"] == out["added"][0]["id"])
    assert stored["source_type"] == "researched" and not stored["verified"] and stored["craft_id"] == "origami"
    assert stored["source_url"] == "https://example.com/diya" and stored["safety_flags"] == []
    assert stored["steps"] == STEPS                                               # concrete steps are kept as they are
    r = pipeline.suggest(d, Request(recipient_id=1, maker_id=1, occasion="Diwali", only_craft="origami"), None, use_llm=False)
    found = [s for s in r["suggestions"] if s.idea_id == stored["id"]]
    assert found and found[0].trust_label == "online"
    assert d.delete_imported_idea(stored["id"])                                   # removable like an import

def _instruction_lines(lines: list[str]) -> list[int]:
    """1 for a line that reads like a real step (an action, enough words), else 0."""
    return [1 if len(l.split()) >= 5 and _VERB.match(l.lstrip("# ")) else 0 for l in lines]


def best_window(text: str, size: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """-> (the stretch of the page, about `size` characters, that holds the most step-like lines, how many it holds).
    Roundup and shop pages score near zero; a real tutorial scores its number of steps."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    hits = _instruction_lines(lines)
    best, best_start, j, chars, run = -1, 0, 0, 0, 0
    for i in range(len(lines)):
        while j < len(lines) and chars + len(lines[j]) + 1 <= size:
            chars += len(lines[j]) + 1
            run += hits[j]
            j += 1
        if run > best:
            best, best_start, best_end = run, i, j
        if j == i:
            j, chars, run = i + 1, 0, 0
            continue
        chars -= len(lines[i]) + 1
        run -= hits[i]
    best = max(best, 0)
    head = lines[0] if lines and best_start > 0 and lines[0].startswith("#") else ""
    return "\\n".join(([head] if head else []) + lines[best_start:best_end])[:size], best

def test_page_window_finds_the_steps_not_the_introduction():
    from app import webpage
    intro = "\n".join(f"A long introduction paragraph number {i} about why paper gifts are lovely to give." for i in range(40))
    text = "# Paper diya\n" + intro + "\n## Steps\n" + "\n".join("- " + x for x in STEPS)
    window, steps = webpage.best_window(text, 700)
    assert steps == 5 and "Cut a 15 cm square" in window and "introduction paragraph number 3" not in window and window.startswith("# Paper diya")
    roundup = "# 100 gifts\n" + "\n".join(f"- Origami idea number {i}" for i in range(60))
    assert webpage.best_window(roundup, 700)[1] == 0                      # a list of names is not a tutorial


def test_read_many_keeps_the_most_tutorial_like_pages(monkeypatch):
    from app import webpage
    pages = {"https://a.example/roundup": "# Top 100\n" + "\n".join(f"- Origami idea number {i} for you" for i in range(60)),
             "https://b.example/how": page(), "https://c.example/err": None}
    def fake_read(u, limit=6000):
        if pages[u] is None:
            raise ValueError("couldn't download that page")
        return pages[u]
    monkeypatch.setattr(webpage, "read", fake_read)
    assert list(webpage.read_many(list(pages))) == ["https://b.example/how"]

<section class="card"><h2>1. Asking for ideas</h2>
<div class="flow">
 <div class="node you"><b>You ask</b>"Something for Maa's birthday". The page also sends who it is for, who is making it and the occasion.</div>
 <div class="node ai"><b>Planner agent</b>Reads the question and picks which tools to call. Up to 7 AI requests and 9 tool calls.</div>
 <div class="node code"><b>15 tools</b>profiles, inventory, crafts, ideas, scoring, calendar, tutorials, shopping gaps, notes, plans, web search, read page, save idea.</div>
 <div class="node code"><b>Rules inside the tools</b>allergies, age, restricted tools, budget, prices, duplicates, skill stretch, occasion fit, variety.</div>
 <div class="node code"><b>Answer check</b>Rejects an answer that used no lookup, or names an idea the tools never returned. The AI retries.</div>
 <div class="node you"><b>Cards shown</b>Only ideas that came back from the tools. The AI writes the short message around them.</div>

 <div class="node code"><b>Search</b>DuckDuckGo from this computer. Shops, video and social sites are skipped.</div>

 <div class="node ai"><b>One AI request</b>Writes each idea in its own words, using only the page text.</div>
 <div class="node code"><b>Step check</b>Rejects vague steps, any size or count not on the page, and steps that don't match the page. Then the normal safety and age checks.</div>
 <div class="node store"><b>Saved</b>Marked "found online" with its source link and removable in one click.</div>
</div>
<p class="rule">No names, allergies, likes or photos of people are ever sent to the AI for this.</p></section>

Everything from your four requests is built, and all 164 tests pass. The server is restarted, and the pipeline diagram is at http://localhost:8765/how. I haven't opened that page in a browser yet.

The diagram has four lanes: - asking for ideas - finding ideas online - reading a photo - finishing a gift

The boxes are colour-coded: you, the AI, plain-code rules, and what's saved on your computer. Here is the same thing in text:

ASK      you → planner agent (Gemini) → 15 tools → fixed rules → answer check → cards
ONLINE   search → read pages → keep the 3 best → one Gemini request → step check → saved
PHOTO    upload → Gemini reads it → clean-up → unsure? ask you : update skills → saved
FINISH   rating + difficulty → "what was hard?" → skill model + taste memory

Why technique lists only cover origami: plan.md says to hand-build one craft's list first. A list needs a crafter's judgement about which techniques exist, how hard each is, and what depends on what. I stopped at origami rather than guess for 24 crafts.

Photo delete - The × button now shows on every photo on the home board, including photos of finished gifts. - Deleting a photo also deletes the saved reading of it. - A gift keeps its history entry when only its photo goes. - Skill changes the photo already caused stay, because they came from a judgement and not from the file.

Regression set - Personas: tests/regression/personas.json has four makers (beginner, intermediate, over-claimer, advanced), each with a sequence of events and the expected direction for every technique. - Photo reader: tests/regression/photo_cases.json has six model outputs it must handle: blurry, invented technique, out-of-range numbers, wrong craft, duplicates, and a clear photo. - Skill-level ranking: a check that nobody is asked to learn more than two new techniques at once. - Live photos: scripts/regress_photos.py checks real photos you label in tests/regression/photos/, at about one free request per photo. It is untested on real photos because the folder is empty. Don't put photos of people there.

Less vague online steps - Before: Gemini wrote steps from search snippets, which are a line or two long. - Now: code searches, downloads the real pages, and keeps the three that look most like step-by-step tutorials. It sends the densest stretch of each. One Gemini request then writes the ideas using only that text. - Checks in code: it rejects vague steps and any size or count that isn't on the page. It also rejects steps that don't match the page, and it drops an idea whose page wasn't read. - Planner path: the planner's own "save online idea" tool must read the page first and goes through the same checks. - Live result: the Birthday Cake tutorial came back with 12 to 14 concrete steps, such as "fold the left and right edges to align with the vertical crease". The gift box tutorial gave the same kind of detail, including the 16x16 cm lid. - Cost: one Gemini request per search instead of up to 6. - Cards: a found idea's card now says "Steps adapted from . The original page has the photos and exact sizes."

Limits - Results vary between runs. Some runs return nothing usable, and one stopped at step 12 of a longer tutorial. I widened the page window afterwards, and the follow-up run had no truncation. - The checks catch invented numbers and filler. They can't tell whether a step is correct, so the original-page link matters. - Pages that need JavaScript, or that are mostly photos, give little text and get skipped. - The ranking barely separates skill levels. The advanced persona still gets the easy panda origami as top pick, because the ranking gives skill only a modest weight. I didn't change that without asking you.

Do you want me to make the ranking weigh skill level more strongly?

def stretch(db: DB, maker_id: int, idea: dict, view: "View | None" = None) -> dict | None:
    """How good a stretch is this idea for this maker? None when the idea has no technique data."""
    techs = tq.for_idea(idea)
    if not techs:
        return None
    view = view or View(db, maker_id)
    known = new = hard = 0
    conf = 0.0
    new_names, hard_names = [], []
    for t in techs:
        level, c = view.estimate(t)
        conf += c
        gap = view.tier(t) - level
        if gap <= KNOWN_GAP:
            known += 1
        elif gap <= NEW_GAP:
            new += 1
            new_names.append(tq.get(t)["name"])
        else:
            hard += 1
            hard_names.append(tq.get(t)["name"])
    conf /= len(techs)
    score = 0.0
    if hard == 0 and new in (1, 2) and known / len(techs) >= 0.5:
        score = 1.5                      # about 80% known plus one or two new: the sweet spot
    elif new == 0 and hard == 0:
        score = -0.4 if conf >= 0.4 else 0.0   # nothing new is boring, unless we are not sure of the level yet
    else:
        score = -min(3.0, 1.0 * hard + max(0, new - 2))   # too many new or a big jump: frustrating
    if conf < 0.3 and (new + hard) > 1:
        score -= 0.5                     # not sure of their level: prefer the safer pick
    return {"score": score, "known": known, "new": new_names, "too_hard": hard_names, "confidence": round(conf, 2)}

Skill level now changes the ranking much more. All 164 tests pass and the server is restarted.

Why it was weak: the penalty for an idea with nothing new to learn only applied once the app was fairly confident about a maker's level. A maker who has only given their own rating never reached that confidence, so easy ideas were never marked down. The penalty was also a flat 0.4 however far above the idea they were.

What I changed (app/skill.py): - Boring penalty: it now grows with how far the maker's level is above the idea's techniques, from 0.4 up to 1.6. - Self-rated makers: the penalty is reduced by a quarter instead of switched off. At the confidence a self-rating gives (0.2), it applies at 75% strength.

Top picks before and after, same inventory and occasion:

Level Before After
0 (beginner) easy panda, bookmarks unchanged
1 easy panda medium dinosaur, medium pop-up panda
2 easy panda medium pop-up panda
3 (advanced) easy panda medium pop-up panda

The regression test now checks two things. A beginner is led with an easy idea and a skilled maker is not. The set of ideas offered also gets harder as skill goes up.

Limits: - Non-origami crafts: the lower-ranked slots for advanced makers still include easy kirigami hearts and letters. Only origami has technique data, so skill can't push those crafts up or down. This is the same gap as the missing technique lists. - Hard origami: it still doesn't win outright for an advanced maker. The hard origami astronaut only reached the level 2 list, at fourth place. I didn't push harder because it would make rankings swing from small skill changes. - Untuned weights: the penalty weights are my judgement and haven't been tried on real use.

"""Reference photos for ideas, looked up on the web for free (DuckDuckGo image search from this machine).

Only the idea's title and craft name are searched, never anything about people. The small preview that comes back
(hosted by Bing) is downloaded once, re-encoded like every other image (so nothing from the web stays in it) and
cached; the card says where the picture came from and links to that page. A failed lookup is remembered for a week so
we don't keep searching. These pictures show what the idea can look like; they are not a promise of how yours turns out."""
import re
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from urllib.parse import urlparse

import httpx

from . import importer
from .core.text import norm
from .db.database import DB

RETRY_AFTER_S = 7 * 86400
THUMB_HOST = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9-]+\.mm\.bing\.net$")       # the only host we download from
STOP = {"gift", "gifts", "handmade", "craft", "crafts", "for", "the", "and", "with", "diy", "make", "making", "easy"}


def _words(text: str) -> set[str]:
    return {w for w in norm(text).split() if len(w) > 2 and w not in STOP}


def _pick(rows: list[dict], idea: dict) -> dict | None:
    """The result whose own title shares the most words with the idea title; none if nothing matches at all."""
    want = _words(idea["title"])
    best, best_n = None, 0
    for r in rows:
        u = urlparse(r.get("thumbnail", ""))
        if u.scheme != "https" or not THUMB_HOST.match(u.hostname or ""):
            continue
        n = len(want & _words(r.get("title", "")))
        if n > best_n:
            best, best_n = r, n
    return best


def _download(url: str) -> bytes | None:
    try:
        r = httpx.get(url, timeout=8, follow_redirects=False, headers={"User-Agent": "GiftBulb/1.0"})
        if r.status_code == 200 and len(r.content) <= 1_000_000 and r.headers.get("content-type", "").startswith("image/"):
            return importer.sanitise(r.content)[0]
    except (httpx.HTTPError, importer.InputError):
        pass
    return None


def search(query: str) -> list[dict]:
    from ddgs import DDGS
    return DDGS().images(query, max_results=8)

s=s[:a]+'''def _from_web(idea: dict) -> dict | None:
    """Network only (safe to run in a thread): search, choose, download. Raises when the search itself is down."""
    pick = _pick(search(f"{idea['title']} {idea.get('craft_name', '')} handmade gift".strip()), idea)
    data = _download(pick["thumbnail"]) if pick else None
    if not data:
        return None
    page = pick.get("url", "")
    return {"data": data, "credit": (urlparse(page).hostname or "").removeprefix("www."), "page": page if page.startswith("https://") else ""}


def _known(db: DB, idea: dict) -> tuple[bool, dict | None]:
    """-> (settled, result): settled means no web lookup is needed (own photo, cached hit, or a recent miss)."""
    if idea.get("images"):
        return True, {"file": idea["images"][0], "credit": idea.get("creator", ""), "page": idea.get("source_url", "")}
    row = db.conn.execute("SELECT created, file FROM idea_images WHERE idea_id=?", (idea["id"],)).fetchone()
    if row and (row["file"] or time.time() - row["created"] < RETRY_AFTER_S):
        return True, cached(db, idea["id"])
    return False, None


def _remember(db: DB, idea: dict, web: dict | None) -> dict | None:
    out = {"file": importer.store(web["data"]), "credit": web["credit"], "page": web["page"]} if web else None
    db.conn.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO idea_images VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)",
                    (idea["id"], out["file"] if out else "", out["page"] if out else "", out["credit"] if out else "", time.time()))
    db.conn.commit()
    return out


def lookup(db: DB, idea: dict) -> dict | None:
    """-> {file, credit, page} or None. Our own photos (imported ideas) win; then the cache; then the web."""
    return lookup_many(db, [idea])[idea["id"]]


def lookup_many(db: DB, ideas: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict | None]:
    """Web lookups run side by side; every database read and write stays on the calling thread."""
    out, todo = {}, []
    for i in ideas:
        settled, res = _known(db, i)
        if settled:
            out[i["id"]] = res
        else:
            todo.append(i)

    def fetch(i):
        try:
            return i, _from_web(i), True
        except Exception:
            return i, None, False                      # search is down: don't remember a failure that isn't the idea's fault

    if todo:
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as pool:
            for i, web, ok in pool.map(fetch, todo):
                out[i["id"]] = _remember(db, i, web) if ok else None
    return out

Reference photos for the top 3 ideas in each craft are built, and the 169 tests pass. I tried it live and have not opened it in a real browser.

How the images work - Where they appear: each craft card on "Find ideas" shows up to 3 pictures with the idea titles, filled in as the card scrolls into view. - Where they come from: a free DuckDuckGo image search using only the idea title and craft name. - Storage: the small preview is downloaded once, re-encoded and saved on your computer. The card links to the source site. - Cards and misses: ideas you open from that craft show the same cached picture. A miss is remembered for a week. - Live check: origami and candle-making both came back with pictures, shown above. The origami ones match well: honeybee, sparrows and a marigold. The candle ones are good except the painted tea-light jars. - Wrong occasion: that picture is red-white-blue star jars with American-flag ribbons, which has nothing to do with Diwali. Matching is only by title words, so the occasion isn't checked. - No agent: I didn't add an AI agent for images, and choosing a picture doesn't need one. An AI check would catch the flag-jar problem, at one free request per picture. Do you want it?

Occasion and trends - Occasion: there's no dedicated tool. The occasion shapes ranking (+3.0 for an idea tagged with it, a penalty for another festival's tag) and goes into the planner's prompt. search_ideas and the research run also mention it. Nothing requires an idea to match the occasion. - Trends: nothing searches for current gifting or craft trends. The web search finds tutorials, not what's popular now.

I haven't built either, because you asked me to check with you before adding features.

I'd suggest adding two planner tools: an occasion brief that looks up the occasion's traditions, colours and typical motifs, and a trends lookup that searches recent gift and craft trends. Each would feed the planner's answer and research prompts, with nothing about people sent, and I'd check any trend idea against the same safety rules. Each lookup costs about one free request and would be cached for a few days. Do you want both tools or just one?

    except plans_mod.PlanError as e:

@router.get("/makers/{maker_id}/skills")
def maker_skills(maker_id: int, r: HttpRequest):
    if not db(r).get("makers", maker_id):
        raise HTTPException(404, "unknown maker")
    return {"craft": skill.tq.craft_id(), "techniques": skill.profile(db(r), maker_id), "area_levels": db(r).skills(maker_id)}


@router.get("/makers/{maker_id}/skill-questions")
def skill_questions(maker_id: int, r: HttpRequest, occasion: str = "", recipient_id: int | None = None):
    """Techniques worth asking about, from the ideas this maker would see right now."""
    if not db(r).get("makers", maker_id):
        raise HTTPException(404, "unknown maker")
    ideas = [i for i in db(r).ideas() if skill.tq.for_idea(i)]
    from .. import pairing
    ideas += [p for p in pairing.generate(db(r).dynamic_motifs()) if p["craft_id"] == skill.tq.craft_id()][:60]
    return {"questions": skill.questions(db(r), maker_id, ideas)}


class SelfReportIn(BaseModel):
    technique: str
    answer: str = Field(pattern="^(never|some|comfortable)$")


@router.post("/makers/{maker_id}/skills/self-report")
def skill_self_report(maker_id: int, s: SelfReportIn, r: HttpRequest):
    if not db(r).get("makers", maker_id) or not skill.tq.get(s.technique):
        raise HTTPException(404, "unknown maker or technique")
    skill.set_self_report(db(r), maker_id, s.technique, s.answer)
    return {"ok": True}


@router.get("/stats")
def stats(r: HttpRequest):
    return plans_mod.stats(db(r))

new='''def craft_id() -> str:
    """The craft with a fully hand-built technique list (recipes and subject rules). Every other craft has a skills list."""
    return _data()["craft_id"]


@lru_cache
def _other() -> list[dict]:
    return json.loads((config.DATA_DIR / "craft_skills_seed.json").read_text())["skills"]


@lru_cache
def all_techniques() -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Origami's techniques plus the skills of every other craft. A skill used by several crafts appears once."""
    out = {t["id"]: {**t, "crafts": [t["craft_id"]]} for t in _data()["techniques"]}
    out.update({t["id"]: t for t in _other()})
    return out


@lru_cache
def _craft_skills() -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    by: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for t in all_techniques().values():
        for c in t["crafts"]:
            by.setdefault(c, []).append(t["id"])
    return {c: sorted(ids, key=lambda i: (all_techniques()[i]["tier"], i)) for c, ids in by.items()}


def craft_skills(craft: str) -> list[str]:
    """Every skill a craft asks for, easiest first."""
    return list(_craft_skills().get(craft, []))


def shared_with(tid: str) -> list[str]:
    """Other crafts that use the same skill: practice in one counts in all of them."""
    return list(all_techniques()[tid]["crafts"])


@lru_cache
def _area_of_craft() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {c["id"]: c["area"] for c in json.loads((config.DATA_DIR / "crafts_seed.json").read_text())}


def areas_of(tid: str) -> set[str]:
    """Craft areas (painting, paper, ...) whose self-reported level says something about this skill."""
    return {_area_of_craft().get(c, c) for c in all_techniques()[tid]["crafts"]}


def get(tid: str) -> dict | None:
    return all_techniques().get(tid)


def for_idea(idea: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Skill ids an idea uses. Origami: from its recipe table or the subject's form. Other crafts: the craft's skills,
    more of them the harder the idea is (easy ideas need the basics only). [] for an unknown craft."""
    d = _data()
    cid = idea.get("craft_id") or idea.get("craft_area")
    if cid != d["craft_id"]:
        skills = craft_skills(idea.get("craft_id") or "")
        if not skills:
            return []
        cutoff = {"easy": 2, "medium": 3}.get(idea.get("difficulty"), 5)
        chosen = [t for t in skills if all_techniques()[t]["tier"] <= cutoff]
        return chosen if len(chosen) >= 2 else skills[:2]
    if idea["id"] in d["recipes"]:
        return list(d["recipes"][idea["id"]])
    if idea.get("tier") == 2:  # a craft x subject pairing: techniques come from the kind of subject and its detail
        form = idea.get("motif_form") or ""
        rules = d["pair_rules"].get(form)
        if not rules:
            return []
        cx = int(idea.get("complexity", 1)) if "complexity" in idea else {"easy": 0, "medium": 1, "hard": 2}.get(idea.get("difficulty"), 1)
        out: list[str] = []
        for level in range(0, min(2, cx) + 1):
            out += rules.get(str(level), [])
        return list(dict.fromkeys(out))
    return []

KNOWN_GAP, NEW_GAP = 0.5, 1.5                      # level within 0.5 of the tier = known; up to 1.5 below = new


def _stats(db: DB, tid: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    r = db.conn.execute("SELECT hard,easy FROM technique_stats WHERE technique_id=?", (tid,)).fetchone()
    return (r["hard"], r["easy"]) if r else (0, 0)


def tier(db: DB, tid: str) -> float:
    return tq.effective_tier(tid, *_stats(db, tid))


def estimate(db: DB, maker_id: int, tid: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
    r = db.conn.execute("SELECT level,confidence FROM skill_estimates WHERE maker_id=? AND technique_id=?", (maker_id, tid)).fetchone()
    if r:
        return r["level"], r["confidence"]
    self_report = _self_report(db.skills(maker_id), tid)
    return PRIOR_LEVEL.get(self_report, PRIOR_LEVEL[1]), PRIOR_CONF


def _save(db: DB, maker_id: int, tid: str, level: float, conf: float) -> None:
    db.conn.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO skill_estimates VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)",
                    (maker_id, tid, max(0.0, min(5.0, level)), max(0.0, min(1.0, conf)), time.time()))
    db.conn.commit()




def _vote(db: DB, tid: str, hard: int = 0, easy: int = 0) -> None:
    db.conn.execute("INSERT INTO technique_stats VALUES(?,0,0) ON CONFLICT(technique_id) DO NOTHING", (tid,))
    db.conn.execute("UPDATE technique_stats SET hard=hard+?, easy=easy+? WHERE technique_id=?", (hard, easy, tid))
    db.conn.commit()


def set_self_report(db: DB, maker_id: int, tid: str, answer: str) -> None:
    """The maker told us: never | some | comfortable. Beats photo guesses (confidence 0.6)."""
    level = {"never": 0.4, "some": 1.8, "comfortable": 3.4}.get(answer)
    if level is None:
        raise ValueError("answer must be never, some or comfortable")
    t = tier(db, tid)
    _save(db, maker_id, tid, min(level, t + 0.6) if answer == "comfortable" else level, 0.6)

def test_every_craft_has_skills_and_shared_skills_cross_crafts():
    import json
    from app import config
    crafts = json.loads((config.DATA_DIR / "crafts_seed.json").read_text())
    for c in crafts:
        skills = tq.craft_skills(c["id"])
        assert len(skills) >= 2, c["id"]
        assert all(i in tq.all_techniques() for i in skills)
    paint = {c["id"] for c in crafts if c["area"] == "painting"}
    assert {"warli-art", "watercolor-wash", "madhubani-art", "pebble-painting"} <= set(tq.shared_with("brush-control"))
    assert len(paint & set(tq.shared_with("brush-control"))) >= 6
    assert set(tq.shared_with("neat-gluing")) >= {"card-making", "paper-mache", "rakhi-making"}


def test_easier_ideas_need_fewer_skills_than_harder_ones():
    easy = tq.for_idea({"id": "a", "craft_id": "watercolor-wash", "difficulty": "easy"})
    hard = tq.for_idea({"id": "b", "craft_id": "watercolor-wash", "difficulty": "hard"})
    assert set(easy) < set(hard) and "wet-on-wet" in hard and "wet-on-wet" not in easy


def test_practice_in_one_craft_counts_in_another_that_shares_the_skill():
    d, m = maker(None)
    watercolor = {"id": "w", "craft_id": "watercolor-wash", "difficulty": "easy"}
    warli = {"id": "x", "craft_id": "warli-art", "difficulty": "easy"}
    before = skill.estimate(d, m, "brush-control")
    skill.apply_completion(d, m, watercolor)
    after = skill.estimate(d, m, "brush-control")
    assert after[0] > before[0] and after[1] > before[1]
    assert "brush-control" in tq.for_idea(warli)                      # warli sees the same, improved skill

def _aliases() -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    from .core.text import norm
    out = {}
    for c in json.loads((config.DATA_DIR / "crafts_seed.json").read_text()):
        out[c["id"]] = {norm(x) for x in (c["id"].replace("-", " "), c["name"], c["search"]) if x}
    out["origami"].add("paper folding")
    return out


def crafts_named(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Which crafts does a free-text craft name (say, from a photo reading) refer to? A vague name ('painting') matches several."""
    from .core.text import norm
    t = norm(text)
    if len(t) < 4:
        return []
    return [c for c, names in _aliases().items() if any(n in t or t in n for n in names)]


def catalog_text() -> str:
    """The skill list for a model prompt: shared skills once, then each craft's own."""
    t = all_techniques()
    lines = ["Shared by several crafts:"] + [f"- {i}: {x['name']}" for i, x in t.items() if len(x["crafts"]) > 1]
    by = {}
    for i, x in t.items():
        if len(x["crafts"]) == 1:
            by.setdefault(x["crafts"][0], []).append(f"- {i}: {x['name']}")
    for craft, rows in by.items():
        lines += [f"{craft}:"] + rows
    return "\\n".join(lines)

# ---- experience and craft-level reading ----
PROVEN_CONFIDENCE = 0.3     # below this a level is mostly our guess from their own rating, so it is not evidence


def experience(db: DB, maker_id: int) -> dict[str, int]:
    """How many things this maker has finished in each craft (from finished gifts)."""
    from . import pipeline
    out: dict[str, int] = {}
    for g in db.conn.execute("SELECT idea_id FROM gifts WHERE maker_id=?", (maker_id,)):
        i = pipeline.find_idea(db, g["idea_id"])
        c = (i or {}).get("craft_id") or (i or {}).get("craft_area")
        if c:
            out[c] = out.get(c, 0) + 1
    return out


def craft_skills(db: DB, maker_id: int, craft_id: str, view: "View | None" = None) -> list[dict]:
    """The skills a craft needs, with this maker's level in each. `proven` = we have real evidence they have it."""
    view = view or View(db, maker_id)
    rows = []
    for tid in tq.craft_skills(craft_id):
        level, conf = view.estimate(tid)
        t = tq.get(tid)

def _with_variety(crafts: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Crafts they have made a lot come first, but never all in a row: familiar crafts are mixed with crafts that build
    on skills they have shown, and with brand-new ones, so there is always something different to pick."""
    familiar = sorted((c for c in crafts if c["made"]), key=lambda c: -c["made"])
    rest = [c for c in crafts if not c["made"]]
    adjacent = sorted((c for c in rest if c["proven_share"] >= 0.3 or len(c["builds_on"]) >= 2), key=lambda c: -c["proven_share"])
    fresh = [c for c in rest if c not in adjacent]            # keeps the ready-first order
    for c in familiar:
        c["why"] = f"You've made {c['made']} of these"
    for c in adjacent:
        c["why"] = "Builds on " + ", ".join(c["builds_on"]).lower() if c["builds_on"] else "Uses skills you've shown"
    for c in fresh:
        c["why"] = "New for you"
    buckets = {"F": familiar, "A": adjacent, "X": fresh}
    out: list[dict] = []
    while any(buckets.values()):

                out.append(buckets[k].pop(0))
    return out

"""Reference photos for ideas, looked up on the web for free (DuckDuckGo image search from this machine).

Only the idea's title and craft are searched, never anything about people. Candidates are first filtered by code
(shop shots, clip art, coloring pages and holiday themes the idea doesn't mention are dropped; titles must share words
with the idea). Then ONE Gemini request looks at the best few and picks the one that really shows this handmade item, or
says none do: a missing picture is better than a wrong one. Without the AI (no quota) only a strong text match is used.
The chosen preview (hosted by Bing) is re-encoded like every other image and cached; the card names and links its source.
These pictures show what the idea can look like; they are not a promise of how yours turns out."""
import re
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from urllib.parse import urlparse

import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from . import importer, pairing
from .core.text import norm
from .db.database import DB

RETRY_AFTER_S = 7 * 86400
VET_PER_DAY = 40                                   # of the free Gemini requests, at most this many go to picking pictures
CANDIDATES = 5
THUMB_HOST = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9-]+\.mm\.bing\.net$")       # the only host we download from
STOP = {"gift", "gifts", "handmade", "craft", "crafts", "for", "the", "and", "with", "diy", "make", "making", "easy", "set", "idea", "ideas"}
BAD_WORDS = {"buy", "sale", "shop", "price", "wholesale", "amazon", "aliexpress", "alibaba", "clipart", "clip", "vector", "svg", "png", "logo",
             "template", "printable", "coloring", "colouring", "stock", "wallpaper", "icon", "cartoon", "emoji", "mockup"}
HOLIDAYS = {"christmas", "halloween", "easter", "thanksgiving", "valentine", "valentines", "patriotic", "independence", "july", "flag", "usa", "american", "xmas", "santa"}


def _words(text: str) -> set[str]:
    return {w for w in norm(text).split() if len(w) > 2 and w not in STOP}


def _craft_terms(idea: dict) -> tuple[str, set[str]]:
    c = next((c for c in pairing.crafts() if c["id"] == idea.get("craft_id")), None)
    return (c["search"], _words(c["search"] + " " + c["name"])) if c else (idea.get("craft_name", ""), _words(idea.get("craft_name", "")))


def query(idea: dict) -> str:
    term, _ = _craft_terms(idea)
    title = idea["title"]
    return f"{title} {term}".strip() if norm(term) not in norm(title) else title      # no doubled craft name


def score(row: dict, idea: dict) -> float:
    """How well a search result's own title fits this idea; <= 0 means do not use it."""
    u = urlparse(row.get("thumbnail", ""))
    if u.scheme != "https" or not THUMB_HOST.match(u.hostname or ""):
        return 0.0
    title_words = _words(row.get("title", ""))
    if title_words & BAD_WORDS:
        return 0.0
    if title_words & HOLIDAYS and not _words(idea["title"] + " " + " ".join(idea.get("tags", []))) & HOLIDAYS:
        return 0.0                                                  # a Christmas or flag-themed picture for a plain idea
    _, craft_words = _craft_terms(idea)
    subject = len(_words(idea["title"]) & title_words)
    return subject * 2.0 + len(craft_words & title_words) + (0.5 if title_words & {"diy", "tutorial", "how"} else 0)

def jpg():
    b = io.BytesIO()
    Image.new("RGB", (60, 40), "orange").save(b, "JPEG")
    return b.getvalue()


def row(title, n, page="https://www.paper.example/panda"):
    return {"title": title, "thumbnail": f"https://ts{n}.mm.bing.net/th?id={n}", "url": page}


IDEA = {"id": "pair-origami-panda", "title": "Origami panda", "craft_id": "origami", "craft_name": "Origami", "tags": []}
GOOD = [row("Origami panda easy tutorial", 1), row("How to fold an origami panda", 2, "https://b.example/p")]


def fake_web(monkeypatch, rows, calls=None):
    def search(q):
        if calls is not None:
            calls.append(q)
        return rows
    monkeypatch.setattr(images, "search", search)
    monkeypatch.setattr(images, "_download", lambda url: jpg() if "mm.bing.net" in url else None)


def test_candidates_are_filtered_by_code_before_anyone_looks_at_them():
    assert images.score(row("Origami panda easy tutorial", 1), IDEA) > 0
    assert images.score(row("Origami panda clipart vector", 1), IDEA) == 0                 # not a photo of a made thing
    assert images.score(row("Buy origami panda for sale", 1), IDEA) == 0                   # a shop listing
    assert images.score(row("Origami panda christmas ornament", 1), IDEA) == 0             # holiday the idea never mentioned
    assert images.score(row("Origami panda christmas ornament", 1), {**IDEA, "tags": ["christmas"]}) > 0
    assert images.score(row("Knitted scarf pattern", 1), IDEA) == 0                        # shares nothing
    assert images.score({"title": "Origami panda", "thumbnail": "https://evil.example/x", "url": "https://x"}, IDEA) == 0   # never downloaded

    assert images.query(IDEA) == "Origami panda"
    assert images.query({"id": "x", "title": "Rolled beeswax", "craft_id": "candle-making"}) == "Rolled beeswax homemade candle"


def test_ai_pick_is_used_credited_and_cached_once(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "PHOTOS_DIR", tmp_path)
    calls, asked = [], []
    fake_web(monkeypatch, GOOD, calls)
    d = mk(PAPER)
    got = images.lookup(d, IDEA, model=vision({"best": 1, "reason": "clear photo of the folded panda"}, asked))

    assert images.lookup(d, IDEA, model=vision({"best": 0}, asked)) is None and len(calls) == 1
    assert not list((tmp_path / "ideas").glob("*.jpg")) if (tmp_path / "ideas").exists() else True       # nothing kept


def test_out_of_range_ai_answer_is_treated_as_none(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

All three changes are built and the 183 tests pass. The server on port 8765 is running the latest code. I checked the data through the API but haven't looked at the pages in a browser.

Pictures - Cause: the old code picked by word overlap with the title, so a flag-themed jar could win for Diwali. - Filtering: the search now uses each craft's own search term. Code drops shop listings, clip art, coloring pages and holiday themes the idea doesn't mention. - Gemini check: Gemini then looks at up to 5 candidates and picks the one that really shows the item, or says none do. A missing picture is better than a wrong one. - Live result on 9 ideas: the rakhis, clay diya, sparrow nest, mandala, toran and rangoli pots, and the candles all fit. One miss, a "clay honeybee" that was an embossed cylinder, got through while Gemini wasn't asked. Picks made without Gemini are now re-checked once it's available. - Cost: one free Gemini request per idea, capped at 40 a day. A craft's first preview takes about 10 to 15 seconds, and later views come from the cache.

Skills per craft and shared skills - Coverage: all 33 crafts now have a skills list, 112 skills in total. 19 are shared across crafts. - Shared skills: for example, "Holding and steering a brush" is used by 9 painting crafts, and "Gluing neatly" by 14 crafts. - Transfer: a skill is one skill per maker, so finishing a watercolour piece raises brush control for Warli and the other painting crafts too. Your own rating of an area, such as painting, sets the starting level for its skills. - Skill lists per idea: for crafts other than origami, an idea's skills come from its difficulty: basics for easy, more for medium, all for hard. They are coarser than origami's per-subject lists, so they count 40% as much in ranking. - Elsewhere: photo reading, "what was hard?" and the maker page use the skills too. The maker page now groups them by craft, with the crafts someone has made first.

Ordering and variety - Craft cards: crafts you've made come first, then crafts that build on skills you've shown, then new ones. The pattern is two familiar, then a mix, so a screenful is never all one kind. Each card says why it's there, for example "You've made 3 of these", and lists its skills with the shared ones marked. - Previews: the top 3 ideas are ranked for the maker's skill level, so they differ by level. Each shows what you'd learn. - Your maker Tanya: she has made nothing yet, so every craft says "New for you" and the order is "ready to make" first. The experience-based ordering is covered by tests only.

Limits - The skill lists are my own, not reviewed by a crafter. Please skim data/craft_skills_seed.json for anything wrong. - The stretch ranking pushed painting out of one test: abstract painting dropped out of the anniversary suggestions for a husband, replaced by a Madhubani rose. I changed that test to accept any painting craft. Abstract painting is still there if you pick that craft. - Pictures are cached per idea, not per occasion.

Two questions are still open from before: the occasion-brief and trends tools, and whether you want those.

# Points to ponder

Decisions and open questions that came up while building Gift Bulb. "Open" means nobody has decided yet.
"Decided" records the answer so it isn't asked again. Newest topics last.

## Open

### 1. Occasion brief and trends tools for the chat agent
Today the occasion only shapes ranking (+3.0 for an idea tagged with it, a penalty for another festival's tag) and goes into the planner's prompt. Nothing requires an idea to match the occasion, and nothing looks up what is popular now.
- Add an **occasion brief** tool: traditions, colours and typical motifs for that occasion, looked up on the web?
- Add a **trends** tool: recent gifting and craft trends?
- Both would cost about one free Gemini request per lookup, cached for a few days, with no personal data sent. Any trend idea would pass the same safety checks.
- Options: both tools, just one, or neither.
- Related: should the occasion be a **hard requirement** (only ideas tagged for it) or stay a strong preference?

### 2. Who reviews the skill lists?
`data/craft_skills_seed.json` (112 skills across 33 crafts, 19 shared) and the origami list are my own, not reviewed by a crafter. The same goes for the recipes and subjects. Who checks tiers, hints and which crafts share a skill?

### 3. How much should the non-origami skill signal count?
Other crafts' skill lists are per craft and difficulty, not per subject, so they count 40% as much as origami's in ranking (`COARSE_WEIGHT` in `app/skill.py`). That number is my judgement and untested on real use. It pushed abstract painting out of one anniversary example. Is 0.4 right, or should skill lists become per-idea for the most-used crafts?

### 4. Sharing the free Gemini quota (150 requests a day)
Chat (2 to 3 per message), photo reading (1 per photo), online research (1 per search) and picture checking (1 per idea, capped at 40 a day) all draw on the same budget. Is the split right? What should win when it runs low?

### 5. Does advanced skill push hard ideas high enough?
After the last change an advanced maker's top picks are medium ideas and the hard origami astronaut appears at fourth place. Boosting hard ideas more would make rankings swing from small skill changes. Is this the right balance?

### 6. Reference pictures
- Pictures are cached per idea, not per occasion.
- The cached copies are small web thumbnails with a credit and link. Are you comfortable keeping local copies for personal use, or should it link only?
- Picture checking by AI is on (1 free request per idea, capped). The alternative is word matching only, which let a wrong picture through once.

### 7. Photos of people
Regression photos stay in `tests/regression/photos/`, which is git-ignored. Gallery photos can be deleted. What about photos of recipients or children: should the app refuse them, blur faces, or leave it to the user?

### 8. Not built yet (offered, not requested)
Occasion pages, a seasonal planning view, kids mode, restore from backup, multi-day schedules.

### 9. Not verified yet
- The app has only been checked with headless screenshots, API calls and tests. Nobody has clicked through it in a real browser, on a phone, or uploaded a real origami photo.
- The "what was hard?" panel, the person-page taste buttons, the calibration buttons and the new craft cards with pictures and skill lists have not been exercised in a browser.
- Photo reading was only tested live on a crude drawing.

## Decided

- **Telegram bot:** not wanted. The web app covers phones and the camera.
- **Agent rewrite rules:** convert the strict rules to agent tools; ask before adding or changing behaviour. Profiles and calendar are kept as the memory structure.
- **Free tier only:** a free Gemini key and free tools (DuckDuckGo for search). Never add a paid service.
- **Privacy to the AI:** names, allergies, likes and photos of people are never sent to the research or search agent.
- **Skill ranking:** weigh skill level more strongly. Done: the "nothing new is boring"

Vercel will probably start this app, but the data won't persist there, so you need to decide about that first.

Settings

Field Value
Application Preset FastAPI. If your list doesn't have it, pick Other.
Root Directory ./
Build Command Leave empty. The preset has no build step.
Output Directory Leave empty. This is not a static site.
Install Command Leave empty. Vercel reads pyproject.toml and uv.lock.

The entrypoint is app/main.py, which defines app. Vercel looks for app/main.py among its default locations, so you should not need a vercel.json. If the deploy can't find the app, add a vercel.json that points to it, and I'll write it.

Environment variables

  • GEMINI_API_KEY is the only one you must set. Set it under Settings → Environment Variables, not in the repo. .env is git-ignored, so the deployed app can't see it. Without the key, the app falls back to its offline mode.
  • GIFT_DB and GIFT_PHOTOS_DIR are optional. They must point to a writable path such as /tmp/gift.db and /tmp/photos. The default data/ folder is read-only on Vercel.
  • Optional tuning: GIFT_AGENT_MODEL and GIFT_RESEARCH_MODEL default to gemini-3.5-flash-lite. You can also set GIFT_GEMINI_PER_DAY, which defaults to 150.

Why persistence is a problem

Vercel functions are serverless. The only writable place is /tmp, which is wiped when an instance recycles, and different requests can hit different instances. These parts of the app will be lost or inconsistent:

  • profiles
  • the calendar and plans
  • the gallery photos
  • the skill history
  • the daily quota counter, which lives in the SQLite settings table

Also, the Gemini quota guard keeps its counts per instance, so you could exceed the free tier.

Because of that, I'd treat Vercel as a demo, not a place to keep real data. To keep real data, you have two options:

  1. Host somewhere with a persistent disk. Fly.io, Railway or Render can run uvicorn with a volume for SQLite and photos. This needs the fewest code changes.
  2. Stay on Vercel and move storage to a hosted database and blob store. Turso or Neon would replace SQLite, and Vercel Blob would replace the photo folder. This is a real rewrite, and per your rule to ask before changing things, I won't start it without your go-ahead.

Which do you want: a throwaway demo on Vercel, or a deployment that keeps your data?

i need a proper hosting with data, doesnt versel work?? what about netlify
Claude's response

Vercel can work, but not as the app is now. Netlify is a worse fit.

Vercel: It runs your code as short-lived functions with no disk that lasts. To keep data there, SQLite would have to be replaced with a hosted database (Turso or Neon, both with free tiers). Photos would move to Vercel Blob. The quota counter and the research and image caches would need the same treatment. That is a real rewrite of app/db, gallery and images, and I'd ask before starting it.

Netlify: It's the same serverless model, and it has no native Python or FastAPI runtime. You'd have to rewrite the app for JavaScript functions, so I'd rule it out.

Free hosts with a disk that lasts (check each one's current terms before relying on it): - Home machine plus a tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel or Tailscale): It's free, the data stays local, and ./run.sh serve works as it is today. The catch is that your machine has to stay on. - Oracle Cloud Always Free VM: It's free with a real persistent disk and runs the app unchanged. Setup is more work: systemd, HTTPS and backups. - Fly.io, Railway, Render: These are the easiest, with a Dockerfile or start command plus a volume. Persistent disks usually need a paid plan or trial credit, which clashes with your free-only rule.

Login: The app has no login. Profiles hold names, allergies and likes, and the gallery holds photos. A public URL would let anyone read them and use up your Gemini quota. Any hosted option needs a password or a private network such as Tailscale in front of it. I'd add that either way.

I recommend the home machine with Tailscale (private, free, no code changes), or an Oracle VM with a login if you want it always on. Which one do you want? I'll write the setup for it, and if you pick Oracle I'll add a minimal login.

Yes, Supabase can hold everything the app needs, and its free tier covers it. It would replace both SQLite and the local photo folder.

How it would map - Database: Supabase Postgres holds the 21 tables, including profiles, makers, recipients, calendar, plans, gifts, skills, the image and research caches, and settings. The settings table also stores the Gemini quota counter, so the daily limit would finally be shared across instances. - Photos: Supabase Storage replaces data/photos. A private bucket holds gallery, gift and reference-picture files. - Hosting: The FastAPI app can then run on Vercel. Serverless is fine once nothing lives on local disk.

How big the change is - About 50 SQL statements in app/db/database.py plus around 50 more across 9 other modules. They use SQLite syntax such as ? placeholders, INSERT OR REPLACE and row_factory, and these need Postgres equivalents. - Four places read or write photo files and need to switch to Storage. - The tests use an in-memory SQLite database. I'd keep SQLite as a local and test backend behind one small interface, so ./run.sh and the 182 tests keep working. Postgres would be an extra backend. - I'd connect with the Supabase Postgres connection string (via the pooler, which serverless needs) and its Storage API, with no new paid service. The new env vars would be DATABASE_URL, SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY.

Two risks - Cold-start and latency: Each request would make network round trips to the database instead of reading a local file. The ideas page makes many queries, so I'd batch them. Gemini already dominates response time. - Login: Even with Supabase, the app has no login. I'd add a simple login, either Supabase Auth or a shared password, and turn on row-level security so the data isn't public. I recommend doing this in the same change.

Proposed plan 1. Add a storage layer with SQLite and Postgres backends. 2. Add Supabase Storage for photos. 3. Add login. 4. Add vercel.json and a deploy guide. 5. Run the full test suite on both backends.

Do you want me to go ahead with all five steps? If so, do you want Supabase Auth with your email, or a single shared password? One thing I need from you is a Supabase project. Create one and send me the project URL, but keep the keys out of chat. You'd put them straight into Vercel and .env.

class Jobs:
    """In-memory job table with ONE worker: the local model can only do one thing at a time on a CPU."""

    def __init__(self, db: DB, llm: LLMClient):
        self.db, self.llm = db, llm
        self.pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)
        self.jobs: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def submit(self, uploads: list[bytes], caption: str, creator: str, source_url: str) -> str:
        caption, creator, source_url = caption.strip()[:1500], creator.strip()[:60], check_url(source_url)
        if not uploads and not caption:
            raise InputError("Add a photo or paste a caption.")
        if len(uploads) > MAX_IMAGES:
            raise InputError(f"Please use at most {MAX_IMAGES} images.")
        pairs = [sanitise(u) for u in uploads]  # raises before anything is stored
        names = [store(s) for s, _ in pairs]
        jid = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
        with self.lock:
            self._prune()
            self.jobs[jid] = {"status": "queued", "images": names, "created": time.time(), "started": None}
        self.pool.submit(self._run, jid, [m for _, m in pairs[:3]], caption, creator, source_url)  # model sees <=3
        return jid

    def _run(self, jid: str, model_imgs: list[bytes], caption: str, creator: str, source_url: str) -> None:
        job = self.jobs[jid]
        job.update(status="reading", started=time.time())
        try:
            if not self.llm.available():
                raise LLMError("local model server not reachable (is `ollama serve` running?)")
            ex = extract(self.llm, images=model_imgs, caption=caption, creator=creator)
            job["draft"] = build_draft(ex, images=job["images"], creator=creator, source_url=source_url,
                                       vocab=vocabulary(self.db))
            job["status"] = "done"
        except LLMError as e:
            job.update(status="failed", error=str(e))
        except Exception as e:  # never leave a job stuck in "reading"
            job.update(status="failed", error=f"unexpected error: {e}")

    def get(self, jid: str) -> dict | None:
        j = self.jobs.get(jid)
        if not j:
            return None
        out = {k: v for k, v in j.items() if k in ("status", "draft", "error", "images")}
        out["elapsed"] = round(time.time() - j["started"], 1) if j.get("started") else 0
        return out

    def discard(self, jid: str) -> None:
        j = self.jobs.pop(jid, None)
        if j:
            delete_images(j["images"])

    def _prune(self) -> None:
        for jid, j in list(self.jobs.items()):
            if time.time() - j["created"] > 3600 and j["status"] in ("done", "failed"):
                self.discard(jid)

IMG_NAME = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{32}\.jpg$")
URL_OK = re.compile(r"^https?://[^\s]{3,500}$")


class InputError(ValueError):
    """User-facing problem with the uploaded input."""


def images_dir():
    d = config.PHOTOS_DIR / "ideas"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def _jpeg(img: Image.Image, px: int, quality: int) -> bytes:
    img = img.copy()
    img.thumbnail((px, px))
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    img.save(buf, "JPEG", quality=quality, optimize=True)
    return buf.getvalue()


def sanitise(raw: bytes) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
    """Validate an upload and re-encode it (drops EXIF/GPS and any hidden payload). -> (stored, for_model)."""
    if len(raw) > MAX_BYTES:
        raise InputError("That image is too large (max 12 MB).")
    try:
        Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw)).verify()
        img = ImageOps.exif_transpose(Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw))).convert("RGB")
    except (UnidentifiedImageError, OSError, Image.DecompressionBombError, SyntaxError) as e:
        raise InputError("That file isn't a readable image (use JPG, PNG or WebP).") from e
    return _jpeg(img, STORE_PX, 82), _jpeg(img, VLM_PX, 80)


def store(stored: bytes) -> str:
    name = uuid.uuid4().hex + ".jpg"
    (images_dir() / name).write_bytes(stored)
    return name


def delete_images(names: list[str]) -> None:
    for n in names:
        if IMG_NAME.match(n):
            (images_dir() / n).unlink(missing_ok=True)


def check_url(url: str) -> str:
    url = (url or "").strip()
    if url and not URL_OK.match(url):
        raise InputError("The link must start with http:// or https://")
    return url

"""Postgres (Supabase) behind the same small surface the app already uses on sqlite3.

The rest of the code calls `db.conn.execute("... ? ...", params)`, `.fetchone()`, `.lastrowid`, `INSERT OR REPLACE`
and so on. Rather than rewrite ~100 statements, this module translates that SQL dialect on the way out, so the same
queries run on sqlite (local, tests) and on Postgres (hosted).

Design points:
- autocommit: every statement is its own transaction, so one failed statement can never poison the next
  (Postgres would otherwise refuse everything until a rollback) and there is no BEGIN round trip.
- a small connection pool, one statement per checkout; results are fetched fully so the connection goes straight
  back. Works through Supabase's pooler (transaction mode, port 6543): server-side prepared statements are off.
- `INSERT ... ` on a table with an `id` column gets `RETURNING id`, which becomes `lastrowid`.
"""
import re
import threading
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, urlencode, urlsplit, urlunsplit

import psycopg
from psycopg.rows import dict_row
from psycopg_pool import ConnectionPool

IntegrityError = psycopg.IntegrityError


# ---- schema knowledge, parsed from the sqlite schema text so there is one source of truth ------------------------
def parse_schema(schema: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """-> {table: {"cols": [...], "pk": [...], "has_id": bool}}"""
    out = {}
    for m in re.finditer(r"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (\w+)\((.*?)\);", schema, re.S):
        name, body = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        parts, depth, cur = [], 0, ""
        for ch in body:
            depth += ch == "("
            depth -= ch == ")"
            if ch == "," and depth == 0:
                parts.append(cur.strip())
                cur = ""
            else:
                cur += ch
        parts.append(cur.strip())
        cols, pk = [], []
        for p in parts:
            if p.upper().startswith("PRIMARY KEY"):
                pk = [c.strip() for c in re.search(r"\((.*)\)", p).group(1).split(",")]
            elif p.upper().startswith("UNIQUE"):
                continue
            else:
                col = p.split()[0]
                cols.append(col)
                if "PRIMARY KEY" in p.upper():
                    pk = [col]
        out[name] = {"cols": cols, "pk": pk, "has_id": "id" in cols and pk == ["id"] and "INTEGER PRIMARY KEY" in body}
    return out


def postgres_schema(schema: str) -> str:
    """The sqlite schema in Postgres spelling: identity ids, double-precision timestamps."""
    s = re.sub(r"\bid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY", "id BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY", schema)
    s = re.sub(r"\bREAL\b", "DOUBLE PRECISION", s)
    return s.replace("INTEGER", "BIGINT")


# ---- SQL translation --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _placeholders(sql: str) -> str:
    """`?` -> `%s`, and a literal `%` -> `%%`, leaving quoted strings alone except for the `%`."""
    out, quote = [], False
    for ch in sql:
        if ch == "'":
            quote = not quote
        if ch == "%":
            out.append("%%")
        elif ch == "?" and not quote:
            out.append("%s")
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out)

_INSERT = re.compile(r"^\s*INSERT\s+INTO\s+(\w+)", re.I)

SCHEMA_VERSION = "1"

    def __init__(self, path: Path | str = config.DB_PATH, url: str = ""):
        self.remote = bool(url)
        self._cache: dict[str, tuple[float, object]] = {}
        if self.remote:
            self.conn = pg.PgConn(url, pg.parse_schema(SCHEMA))
            self._ensure_remote_schema()
        else:
            if str(path) != ":memory:":
                Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            self.conn = sqlite3.connect(str(path), check_same_thread=False)
            self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            self.conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
            self.conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
            self.conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
            if "photo" not in {r["name"] for r in self.conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(gifts)")}:
                self.conn.execute("ALTER TABLE gifts ADD COLUMN photo TEXT DEFAULT ''")  # older databases
            if "repeat" not in {r["name"] for r in self.conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(occasions)")}:
                self.conn.execute("ALTER TABLE occasions ADD COLUMN repeat TEXT DEFAULT ''")
            if "how" not in {r["name"] for r in self.conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(idea_images)")}:
                self.conn.execute("ALTER TABLE idea_images ADD COLUMN how TEXT DEFAULT ''")   # pictures chosen before they were checked
        self.seed()

    @classmethod
    def open(cls) -> "DB":
        """The configured database: Supabase/Postgres when DATABASE_URL is set, otherwise the local sqlite file."""
        return cls(config.DB_PATH, url=config.DATABASE_URL)

    def _ensure_remote_schema(self) -> None:
        """One cheap query on a warm database; the tables are only created the first time (or after an upgrade)."""
        have = self.conn.execute("SELECT to_regclass('public.settings') AS t").fetchone()["t"]
        if have and self.get_setting("schema_version") == SCHEMA_VERSION:
            return
        self.conn.executescript(pg.postgres_schema(SCHEMA))
        for t in pg.parse_schema(SCHEMA):      # the browser-side API keys must never reach these tables
            self.conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE {t} ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY")
        self.set_setting("schema_version", SCHEMA_VERSION)

    def _cached(self, key: str, load):
        """Remote round trips are the slow part, so read-mostly tables are kept briefly in memory."""
        if not self.remote:
            return load()
        hit = self._cache.get(key)
        if hit and time.time() - hit[0] < CACHE_TTL:
