"""Where photo files live: a folder on this machine, or a private Supabase Storage bucket when one is configured.

Keys look like "ideas/<uuid>.jpg". The database only stores the file name; the browser asks `/photos/<key>`, which the
app serves (behind the login) from whichever backend is active, so the bucket never needs to be public."""
import threading
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from . import config


class StorageError(RuntimeError):
    pass


class LocalStorage:
    def __init__(self, root: Path | None = None):
        self.root = root

    def _path(self, key: str) -> Path:
        root = self.root or config.PHOTOS_DIR
        p = (root / key).resolve()
        if root.resolve() not in p.parents:
            raise StorageError("bad path")
        return p

    def put(self, key: str, data: bytes, content_type: str = "image/jpeg") -> None:
        p = self._path(key)
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_bytes(data)

    def get(self, key: str) -> bytes | None:
        try:
            return self._path(key).read_bytes()
        except (OSError, StorageError):
            return None

    def exists(self, key: str) -> bool:
        try:
            return self._path(key).is_file()
        except StorageError:
            return False

    def delete(self, keys: list[str]) -> None:
        for k in keys:
            try:
                self._path(k).unlink(missing_ok=True)
            except StorageError:
                pass


class SupabaseStorage:
    """Supabase Storage over its REST API with the service key (server side only; the browser never sees it)."""

    def __init__(self, url: str, key: str, bucket: str, client: httpx.Client | None = None):
        self.base, self.bucket = url.rstrip("/") + "/storage/v1", bucket
        self.http = client or httpx.Client(timeout=20, headers={"apikey": key, "Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"})
        self._ready = False
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def _ensure_bucket(self) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            if self._ready:
                return
            r = self.http.post(f"{self.base}/bucket", json={"id": self.bucket, "name": self.bucket, "public": False})
            if r.status_code >= 300 and "already exists" not in r.text and r.status_code != 409:
                raise StorageError(f"could not create the storage bucket ({r.status_code}): {r.text[:200]}")
            self._ready = True

    def put(self, key: str, data: bytes, content_type: str = "image/jpeg") -> None:
        self._ensure_bucket()
        r = self.http.post(f"{self.base}/object/{self.bucket}/{key}", content=data,
                           headers={"Content-Type": content_type, "x-upsert": "true"})
        if r.status_code >= 300:
            raise StorageError(f"upload failed ({r.status_code}): {r.text[:200]}")

    def get(self, key: str) -> bytes | None:
        r = self.http.get(f"{self.base}/object/authenticated/{self.bucket}/{key}")
        return r.content if r.status_code == 200 else None

    def exists(self, key: str) -> bool:
        r = self.http.head(f"{self.base}/object/authenticated/{self.bucket}/{key}")
        return r.status_code == 200

    def delete(self, keys: list[str]) -> None:
        if keys:
            self.http.request("DELETE", f"{self.base}/object/{self.bucket}", json={"prefixes": keys})


_current = None


def current():
    """The active backend. Chosen once; tests swap it with `use()`."""
    global _current
    if _current is None:
        _current = (SupabaseStorage(config.SUPABASE_URL, config.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, config.STORAGE_BUCKET)
                    if config.SUPABASE_URL and config.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY else LocalStorage())
    return _current


def use(backend) -> None:
    global _current
    _current = backend

"""Login with Supabase Auth (e-mail + password), then our own signed cookie so later requests need no network.

Why a cookie of our own: checking a Supabase token on every request would add a round trip to every page. After one
successful Supabase sign-in we issue a signed, expiring, httpOnly cookie. Only e-mails in GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS get in,
so a stranger who signs up directly on the Supabase project still cannot use this app."""
import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import time

import httpx

from . import config

COOKIE = "gb_session"
OPEN_PATHS = ("/login", "/api/auth/", "/assets/", "/favicon.ico")


class AuthError(ValueError):
    """A problem the person can read and fix."""


def _b64(b: bytes) -> str:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(b).decode().rstrip("=")


def _unb64(s: str) -> bytes:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(s + "=" * (-len(s) % 4))


def _mac(body: str) -> str:
    return _b64(hmac.new(config.SESSION_SECRET.encode(), body.encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest())


def make_token(email: str, now: float | None = None) -> str:
    body = _b64(json.dumps({"e": email, "x": int((now or time.time()) + config.SESSION_DAYS * 86400)}).encode())
    return f"{body}.{_mac(body)}"


def read_token(token: str, now: float | None = None) -> str | None:
    """-> the e-mail, or None for anything forged, expired or no longer allowed."""
    try:
        body, mac = token.split(".", 1)
        if not config.SESSION_SECRET or not hmac.compare_digest(mac, _mac(body)):
            return None
        data = json.loads(_unb64(body))
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return None
    if data.get("x", 0) < (now or time.time()):
        return None
    email = str(data.get("e", "")).lower()
    return email if allowed(email) else None


def allowed(email: str) -> bool:
    return bool(email) and email.lower() in config.ALLOWED_EMAILS


def is_open(path: str) -> bool:
    return path == "/login" or any(path.startswith(p) for p in OPEN_PATHS[1:])


def check_setup() -> str:
    """'' when login can work, otherwise what is missing."""
    if not config.ALLOWED_EMAILS:
        return "Login is on but GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS is empty. Set it to your e-mail address (comma-separated for more)."
    if not config.SESSION_SECRET:
        return "Set GIFT_SESSION_SECRET (any long random text) so sign-ins can be remembered."
    if not (config.SUPABASE_URL and config.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY):
        return "SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are needed for login."
    return ""


def _fail(r: httpx.Response, fallback: str) -> AuthError:
    try:
        j = r.json()
        msg = j.get("error_description") or j.get("msg") or j.get("message") or ""
    except ValueError:
        msg = ""
    if "invalid login" in msg.lower():
        msg = "That e-mail and password don't match."
    return AuthError(msg or fallback)


def _clean(email: str, password: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    email = (email or "").strip().lower()
    if "@" not in email or len(email) > 200:
        raise AuthError("Enter a valid e-mail address.")
    if not allowed(email):
        raise AuthError("This e-mail isn't on the list of people allowed to use this app.")
    return email, password or ""


def login(email: str, password: str, client: httpx.Client | None = None) -> str:
    """Check the password with Supabase. -> a session token."""
    email, password = _clean(email, password)
    if problem := check_setup():
        raise AuthError(problem)
    http = client or httpx.Client(timeout=15)
    try:
        r = http.post(f"{config.SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/token", params={"grant_type": "password"},
                      headers={"apikey": config.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY}, json={"email": email, "password": password})
    except httpx.HTTPError as e:
        raise AuthError("Couldn't reach the sign-in service. Try again in a moment.") from e
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise _fail(r, "Sign-in failed.")
    return make_token(email)

"""Sign in / sign up / sign out. These paths are open; everything else needs the session cookie (see main.py)."""
from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Request, Response
from fastapi.concurrency import run_in_threadpool
from pydantic import BaseModel

from .. import auth, config

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth")


class Credentials(BaseModel):
    email: str
    password: str


def _set_cookie(request: Request, response: Response, token: str) -> None:
    secure = request.url.scheme == "https" or request.headers.get("x-forwarded-proto") == "https"
    response.set_cookie(auth.COOKIE, token, max_age=config.SESSION_DAYS * 86400, httponly=True, samesite="lax",
                        secure=secure, path="/")


@router.post("/login")
async def login(c: Credentials, request: Request, response: Response):
    try:
        token = await run_in_threadpool(auth.login, c.email, c.password)
    except auth.AuthError as e:
        raise HTTPException(401, str(e))
    _set_cookie(request, response, token)
    return {"ok": True, "email": c.email.strip().lower()}


@router.post("/signup")
async def signup(c: Credentials, request: Request, response: Response):
    try:
        token = await run_in_threadpool(auth.signup, c.email, c.password)
    except auth.AuthError as e:
        raise HTTPException(400, str(e))
    _set_cookie(request, response, token)
    return {"ok": True, "email": c.email.strip().lower()}


@router.post("/logout")
def logout(response: Response):
    response.delete_cookie(auth.COOKIE, path="/")
    return {"ok": True}


@router.get("/me")
def me(request: Request):
    """Used by the login page and the header. Open on purpose: it only says whether you are signed in."""
    if not config.AUTH_ON:
        return {"auth": False, "email": ""}
    email = auth.read_token(request.cookies.get(auth.COOKIE, ""))
    return {"auth": True, "email": email or "", "problem": auth.check_setup()}

@router.post("/import", status_code=202)
async def import_start(r: HttpRequest, files: list[UploadFile] = File(default=[]), caption: str = Form(""),
                       creator: str = Form(""), source_url: str = Form("")):
    raws = [await f.read(importer.MAX_BYTES + 1) for f in files[:importer.MAX_IMAGES + 1]]
    try:
        return {"job_id": jobs(r).submit(raws, caption, creator, source_url)}
    except importer.InputError as e:
        raise HTTPException(422, str(e))


@router.get("/import/{job_id}")
def import_status(job_id: str, r: HttpRequest):
    j = jobs(r).get(job_id)
    if not j:
        raise HTTPException(404, "unknown or expired import")
    return j


@router.delete("/import/{job_id}", status_code=204)
def import_discard(job_id: str, r: HttpRequest):
    jobs(r).discard(job_id)

sub('app/web/assets/js/common.js',"const signOut=",'''/* Hosting limits a request to about 4 MB, and phone photos are bigger: shrink in the browser first (long side 1600px). */
const shrink=f=>new Promise(res=>{
  if(!f||!f.type.startsWith('image/')||f.size<900e3)return res(f);
  const img=new Image(),u=URL.createObjectURL(f);
  img.onload=()=>{const k=Math.min(1,1600/Math.max(img.width,img.height)),c=document.createElement('canvas');
    c.width=Math.round(img.width*k);c.height=Math.round(img.height*k);c.getContext('2d').drawImage(img,0,0,c.width,c.height);
    URL.revokeObjectURL(u);c.toBlob(b=>res(b&&b.size<f.size?new File([b],'photo.jpg',{type:'image/jpeg'}):f),'image/jpeg',.85)};
  img.onerror=()=>{URL.revokeObjectURL(u);res(f)};img.src=u});
const signOut=''')

cat > scripts/setup_supabase.py <<'EOF'
"""One-time (and safe to repeat) check + setup of the Supabase project this app uses.

   ./run.sh supabase                      check everything and create what is missing
   ./run.sh supabase you@example.com      ...and create (or reset) that login, asking for the password

Creates: the tables (with row-level security on, so the browser-side key can read nothing), the private photo bucket.
Prints one line per check and what to fix. Never prints a key."""
import getpass
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
from app import auth, config, storage  # noqa: E402
from app.db.database import DB  # noqa: E402

bad = 0


def say(ok: bool | None, what: str, fix: str = "") -> None:
    global bad
    bad += ok is False
    print(("  ok   " if ok else "  FIX  " if ok is False else "  --   ") + what + (f"\n         -> {fix}" if fix and not ok else ""))


say(bool(config.SUPABASE_URL), "SUPABASE_URL set", "Project Settings > API > Project URL")
say(bool(config.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY), "SUPABASE_ANON_KEY set", "Project Settings > API > anon / publishable key")
say(bool(config.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY), "SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY set", "Project Settings > API > service_role / secret key (server only)")
say(bool(config.DATABASE_URL), "DATABASE_URL set", "Connect > Transaction pooler; put your database password in it")
say(bool(config.ALLOWED_EMAILS), "GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS set", "your e-mail address; only listed people can sign in")

        t = time.time()
        db.conn.execute("SELECT 1")
        say(None, f"one query round trip: {(time.time() - t) * 1000:.0f} ms (the app keeps this count low; under ~80 ms is typical)")
    except Exception as e:
        say(False, f"database: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:160]}",
            "check the password and that you used the pooler string (port 6543); the direct host needs IPv6")
if config.SUPABASE_URL and config.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY:
    try:
        s = storage.current()
        s.put("ideas/_setup_check.txt", b"ok", "text/plain")
        ok = s.get("ideas/_setup_check.txt") == b"ok"
        s.delete(["ideas/_setup_check.txt"])
        say(ok, f"photo bucket '{config.STORAGE_BUCKET}' private and writable")
    except Exception as e:

    except httpx.HTTPError:
        say(False, "Supabase Auth reachable", "check SUPABASE_URL")

if len(sys.argv) > 1:
    email = sys.argv[1].strip().lower()
    if not auth.allowed(email):
        say(False, f"{email} is not in GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS", "add it there first")
    else:
        pw = getpass.getpass("Password for the new login (8+ characters): ")
        try:

def tr(sql):

def test_schema_knowledge_is_read_from_the_one_sqlite_schema():
    assert TABLES["settings"]["pk"] == ["key"] and TABLES["skill_estimates"]["pk"] == ["maker_id", "technique_id"]
    assert TABLES["plans"]["has_id"] and not TABLES["settings"]["has_id"] and not TABLES["maker_skills"]["has_id"]
    assert len(TABLES) >= 20
    ddl = pg.postgres_schema(SCHEMA)
    assert "GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY" in ddl and "DOUBLE PRECISION" in ddl and "INTEGER" not in ddl


def test_placeholders_and_percent_signs():
    sql, ret = tr("SELECT * FROM gifts WHERE note LIKE '%x%' AND id=? AND idea_id='what?'")
    assert sql == "SELECT * FROM gifts WHERE note LIKE '%%x%%' AND id=%s AND idea_id='what?'" and not ret


def test_insert_or_replace_becomes_an_upsert_on_the_real_key():
    sql, _ = tr("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO settings VALUES(?,?)")
    assert sql == "INSERT INTO settings(key,value) VALUES(%s,%s) ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value=EXCLUDED.value"
    sql, _ = tr("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO skill_estimates VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)")
    assert "ON CONFLICT(maker_id,technique_id) DO UPDATE SET level=EXCLUDED.level,confidence=EXCLUDED.confidence" in sql
    sql, _ = tr("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO maker_skills VALUES(?,?,?)")
    assert "ON CONFLICT(maker_id,craft_area) DO UPDATE SET level=EXCLUDED.level" in sql

    assert "RETURNING" not in sql and not ret
    assert not tr("INSERT INTO settings VALUES(?,?)")[1]          # no id column, nothing to return

PRIOR_LEVEL = {0: 0.6, 1: 1.6, 2: 2.6, 3: 3.6}   # self-report 0-3 -> level
PRIOR_CONF = 0.2
COARSE_WEIGHT = 0.4
KNOWN_GAP, NEW_GAP = 0.5, 1.5                      # level within 0.5 of the tier = known; up to 1.5 below = new


def _stats(db: DB, tid: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    r = db.conn.execute("SELECT hard,easy FROM technique_stats WHERE technique_id=?", (tid,)).fetchone()
    return (r["hard"], r["easy"]) if r else (0, 0)


def tier(db: DB, tid: str) -> float:
    return tq.effective_tier(tid, *_stats(db, tid))


def estimate(db: DB, maker_id: int, tid: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
    r = db.conn.execute("SELECT level,confidence FROM skill_estimates WHERE maker_id=? AND technique_id=?", (maker_id, tid)).fetchone()
    if r:
        return r["level"], r["confidence"]
    self_report = _self_report(db.skills(maker_id), tid)
    return PRIOR_LEVEL.get(self_report, PRIOR_LEVEL[1]), PRIOR_CONF


def _self_report(areas: dict, tid: str) -> int | None:
    """The maker's own 0-3 rating of the craft areas that use this skill (the best of them), if they gave one."""
    given = [areas[a] for a in tq.areas_of(tid) if areas.get(a) is not None]
    return max(given) if given else None


def _save(db: DB, maker_id: int, tid: str, level: float, conf: float) -> None:
    db.conn.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO skill_estimates VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)",
                    (maker_id, tid, max(0.0, min(5.0, level)), max(0.0, min(1.0, conf)), time.time()))
    db.conn.commit()


def _move(db: DB, maker_id: int, tid: str, target: float, weight: float, *, lower: bool = False) -> dict | None:
    """Move the level toward `target` by `weight`. Raises by default; `lower=True` only ever lowers (too hard)."""
    level, conf = estimate(db, maker_id, tid)
    new = level + (target - level) * weight
    new = min(level, new) if lower else max(level, new)   # success only raises; hard / rough work only lowers
    new_conf = conf + (1 - conf) * min(1.0, weight * 0.8)
    _save(db, maker_id, tid, new, new_conf)
    if abs(new - level) < 0.05 and abs(new_conf - conf) < 0.02:
        return None
    return {"technique": tid, "name": tq.get(tid)["name"], "from": round(level, 1), "to": round(new, 1)}

# ---- reading it back ----
def profile(db: DB, maker_id: int) -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for tid, t in tq.all_techniques().items():
        level, conf = estimate(db, maker_id, tid)
        rows.append({"id": tid, "name": t["name"], "tier": round(tier(db, tid), 1), "level": round(level, 1),
                     "confidence": round(conf, 2), "hint": t["hint"], "prereqs": t["prereqs"]})
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r["tier"], r["name"]))


class View:
    """A maker's skills loaded once, so ranking hundreds of ideas costs a handful of queries, not thousands."""

    def __init__(self, db: DB, maker_id: int):
        self.rows = {r["technique_id"]: (r["level"], r["confidence"]) for r in
                     db.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM skill_estimates WHERE maker_id=?", (maker_id,))}
        self.votes = {r["technique_id"]: (r["hard"], r["easy"]) for r in db.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM technique_stats")}
        self.areas = db.skills(maker_id)

    def estimate(self, tid: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
        if tid in self.rows:
            return self.rows[tid]
        return PRIOR_LEVEL.get(_self_report(self.areas, tid), PRIOR_LEVEL[1]), PRIOR_CONF

    def tier(self, tid: str) -> float:
        return tq.effective_tier(tid, *self.votes.get(tid, (0, 0)))


def stretch(db: DB, maker_id: int, idea: dict, view: "View | None" = None) -> dict | None:
    """How good a stretch is this idea for this maker? None when the idea has no technique data."""
    techs = tq.for_idea(idea)
    if not techs:
        return None
    view = view or View(db, maker_id)
    known = new = hard = 0
    conf = margin = 0.0
    new_names, hard_names = [], []
    if (idea.get("craft_id") or idea.get("craft_area")) != tq.craft_id():
        score *= COARSE_WEIGHT           # other crafts' skill lists are per craft and difficulty, not per subject: a weaker signal
    return {"score": score, "known": known, "new": new_names, "too_hard": hard_names, "confidence": round(conf, 2)}


def questions(db: DB, maker_id: int, ideas: list[dict], limit: int = 2) -> list[dict]:
    """Techniques worth asking about: low confidence and used by the ideas on screen."""
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    for idea in ideas:
        for t in tq.for_idea(idea):
            if estimate(db, maker_id, t)[1] < 0.3:
                seen[t] = seen.get(t, 0) + 1
    top = sorted(seen, key=lambda t: (tq.get(t)["tier"] == 1, -seen[t], tq.get(t)["tier"]))[:limit]  # basic folds tell us least: ask about those last
    return [{"technique": t, "name": tq.get(t)["name"], "hint": tq.get(t)["hint"],
             "question": f"Have you done a {tq.get(t)['name'].lower()} before? ({tq.get(t)['hint']})"} for t in top]


def grow_area(db: DB, maker_id: int, idea: dict) -> dict | None:
    """Finishing enough projects in a craft area lifts the maker's 0-3 level there (never lowers it)."""
    from . import pipeline
    area = idea.get("craft_area") or ""
    if not area:
        return None
    done = 0
    for g in db.conn.execute("SELECT idea_id FROM gifts WHERE maker_id=?", (maker_id,)):
        i = pipeline.find_idea(db, g["idea_id"])
        done += bool(i and (i.get("craft_area") == area))
    target = max([lvl for lvl, need in AREA_LEVEL_AT.items() if done >= need] or [0])
    cur = db.skills(maker_id).get(area)
    if target > (cur if cur is not None else 1):
        db.set_skill(maker_id, area, target)
        return {"area": area, "from": cur if cur is not None else 1, "to": target, "finished": done}
    return None

    """Put every table of ours in its own schema, so the app can share a Supabase project with other apps without

    if not schema:

from .db.database import DB

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    app.state.db = DB.open()  # read at start-up, so tests can point it at a temp file
    app.state.db.backfill_motif_crafts(lambda m, pool: pairing.assign_crafts(m, pairing.static_motifs() + pool))
    app.state.guard = QuotaGuard(app.state.db)
    # hosted Gemini (free tier) when a key is set; the old local model client only as a fallback
    app.state.llm = GeminiClient(guard=app.state.guard) if config.GEMINI_API_KEY else LLMClient()
    app.state.jobs = Jobs(app.state.db, app.state.llm)
    # load the model in the background so the first real request is not a cold start (no threads outlive a serverless call)
    if not config.SERVERLESS:
        threading.Thread(target=lambda: app.state.llm.available() and app.state.llm.warm_up(), daemon=True).start()
    yield

def init_state(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Open the database and build the helpers, once. Called at start-up and, as a safety net, on the first request:
    some serverless hosts never run the ASGI start-up step."""
    with _init_lock:
        if getattr(app.state, "ready", False):
            return
        app.state.db = DB.open()  # read at start-up, so tests can point it at a temp file
        app.state.db.backfill_motif_crafts(lambda m, pool: pairing.assign_crafts(m, pairing.static_motifs() + pool))
        app.state.guard = QuotaGuard(app.state.db)
        # hosted Gemini (free tier) when a key is set; the old local model client only as a fallback
        app.state.llm = GeminiClient(guard=app.state.guard) if config.GEMINI_API_KEY else LLMClient()
        app.state.jobs = Jobs(app.state.db, app.state.llm)
        # load the model in the background so the first real request is not a cold start (no threads outlive a serverless call)
        if not config.SERVERLESS:
            threading.Thread(target=lambda: app.state.llm.available() and app.state.llm.warm_up(), daemon=True).start()
        app.state.ready = True


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    app.state.ready = False          # a new app object per test: never trust state left by an earlier one
    init_state(app)
    yield

cat > DEPLOY.md <<'EOF'
# Deploying Gift Bulb (Vercel + Supabase)

Everything the app stores lives in your Supabase project; Vercel only runs the code.

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| profiles, calendar, plans, skills, caches, settings | Supabase Postgres, in its own schema `giftbulb` |
| photos | Supabase Storage, private bucket `gift-bulb-photos` |
| login | Supabase Auth (e-mail + password), limited to `GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS` |

A separate Supabase project is **not** required: the tables sit in their own schema, so they never touch anything else
in the project. (A separate project is still the tidiest choice if you want to delete it later in one click.)

## 1. Environment variables (Vercel > Settings > Environment Variables, and `.env` locally)

| Name | Needed | Where to find it |
|---|---|---|
| `SUPABASE_URL` | yes | Project Settings > API > Project URL (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` also works) |
| `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | yes | Project Settings > API > anon / publishable key (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` also works) |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` | yes | Project Settings > API > service_role / secret key (`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` also works). Server only |
| `DATABASE_URL` | yes | Connect > **Transaction pooler** (port 6543). Put your database password in it. Use the pooler string: the direct one needs IPv6, which Vercel lacks. (`POSTGRES_URL` also works, which is what Vercel's Supabase integration sets) |
| `GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS` | yes | Your e-mail, comma-separated for more people. Nobody else can get in, even if they sign up on the Supabase project directly |
| `GIFT_SESSION_SECRET` | recommended | Any long random text. If empty, the service key is used |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | optional | Free key from Google AI Studio. Without it the app uses its offline rules |
| `GIFT_DB_SCHEMA` | no | Default `giftbulb` |
| `GIFT_BUCKET` | no | Default `gift-bulb-photos` |

Keys in `.env` alone do **not** move a local run to Supabase. The switch is `DATABASE_URL` (or running on Vercel): until
it is set, `./run.sh serve` keeps using the local sqlite file and photo folder, with no login.

## 2. Check and prepare Supabase (safe to repeat)

    ./run.sh supabase                    # creates the tables and the private bucket, then checks everything
    ./run.sh supabase you@example.com    # also creates your login (asks for a password)

If you would rather click: the tables are created automatically the first time the app connects, and you can create
the user under Authentication > Users (tick "Auto Confirm User").

## 3. Vercel

1. Import the GitHub repo. Application Preset: **FastAPI** (or Other). Build / Output / Install: leave empty.
2. Add the variables above. 3. Deploy. `vercel.json` sets a 120 s limit for the AI chat; the Hobby plan allows it with
   Fluid Compute (the default for new projects). If your plan caps functions at 60 s, lower `maxDuration`.

## Notes

- Photos from phones are shrunk in the browser (long side 1600 px) because Vercel limits a request to about 4.5 MB.
- Every query to a remote database costs a network round trip, so read-mostly tables (ideas, prices) are kept in memory
  for 30 s and pages load their data in a handful of queries. `./run.sh supabase` prints your measured round trip.
- Run the whole test suite against a real Postgres: `GIFT_TEST_PG=1 ./run.sh test`.

Do you need a separate Supabase project?

No. The app's tables go in their own Postgres schema, giftbulb, and photos go in their own bucket, so nothing else in the project is touched. A separate project is still tidier if you want to delete everything in one click. The login accounts are shared with any other app in that project, which is why sign-in is limited to an email list.

What I added

  • Database: all your data (profiles, calendar, plans, skills, caches, settings) goes to Supabase Postgres. I did not rewrite the 100 or so queries. They are translated for Postgres on the way out, so the same code runs on SQLite and Postgres.
  • Photos: they move to a private Supabase Storage bucket, gift-bulb-photos, and are served only to signed-in users. Photos are shrunk in the browser first, because Vercel rejects requests over about 4.5 MB.
  • Login: Supabase email and password at /login, with a Sign out link. Only emails in GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS can get in. Creating an account on the login page is off by default, because anyone who knew your email could register it before you.
  • Speed: pages now make far fewer database calls. For example, the maker profile page went from 343 queries to 10. I also cache the ideas and price lists for 10 seconds and skip the start-up seeding when nothing changed.
  • Vercel: index.py, vercel.json (120 s limit), .vercelignore, .env.example and DEPLOY.md are in place. In the Vercel form, choose the FastAPI preset (or "Other") and leave Build, Output and Install empty.
  • Setup check: ./run.sh supabase checks every setting and creates the tables and bucket. ./run.sh supabase you@example.com also creates your login.

What I checked against your project

I read the three Supabase keys from .env, as you said. The photo bucket was created and tested for upload and delete, and the login service is reachable.

What I need from you

  1. DATABASE_URL: in Supabase, open Connect, choose the Transaction pooler string (port 6543), put your database password in it, and add it to .env and Vercel. Without it, the tables are not created in your project. Locally, the keys alone do not switch the app to Supabase.
  2. GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS: your email address, in .env and Vercel.
  3. After that, run ./run.sh supabase you@example.com, then deploy.

Turn 56

i went to connect, what is transaction puller string. i dont see it...
Claude's response

"Transaction pooler" is Supabase's name for one of three ways to connect to the database. Supabase changes its dashboard often, so your screen may look a little different from this.

Where to find it 1. Open your project and click Connect at the top of the page. 2. Choose the Direct tab. Some versions call it Connection String or ORMs. 3. Find the dropdown named Method or Connection method. It offers Direct connection, Transaction pooler and Session pooler. 4. Pick Transaction pooler. The string shown looks like this: postgresql://postgres.abcdefgh:[YOUR-PASSWORD]@aws-0-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres

If you can't find the dropdown - Go to Project Settings → Database. The Connection string section there has the same options. - If you only see a string that starts with db.xxxx.supabase.co:5432, that is the Direct one. It won't work from Vercel, so don't use it. - You can also build the string yourself: postgresql://postgres.PROJECTREF:PASSWORD@aws-0-REGION.pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres PROJECTREF is the part of your project URL before .supabase.co. REGION is shown under Project Settings → General. If you're unsure of the region, copy the string from the dashboard instead.

The password - Replace [YOUR-PASSWORD] with your database password. This is not the API key. You chose it when you created the project. - If you've forgotten it, go to Project Settings → Database → Reset database password. - If the password contains characters like @, / or #, either pick a simpler one or tell me, and I'll show you how to encode it.

Next steps 1. Put the string in .env as DATABASE_URL=... on one line, and add GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS=your@email. 2. Run ./run.sh supabase. It will create the tables and tell you if anything's wrong.

Don't paste the string or password here. If something fails, tell me which line of the check shows FIX and I'll work out the cause.

def test_stored_photos_are_webp_and_smaller_while_the_model_gets_a_jpeg():
    import io
    import random
    from PIL import Image
    from app import importer
    rnd = random.Random(1)
    im = Image.new("RGB", (1600, 1200))
    im.putdata([(rnd.randrange(60, 200), (x // 7) % 255, (x // 5) % 255) for x in range(1600 * 1200)])
    buf = io.BytesIO(); im.save(buf, "JPEG", quality=90)
    stored, for_model = importer.sanitise(buf.getvalue())
    assert Image.open(io.BytesIO(stored)).format == "WEBP" and Image.open(io.BytesIO(for_model)).format == "JPEG"
    assert max(Image.open(io.BytesIO(stored)).size) <= importer.STORE_PX
    assert len(stored) < len(importer._jpeg(Image.open(io.BytesIO(buf.getvalue())).convert("RGB"), importer.STORE_PX, 82))
    name = importer.store(stored)
    assert name.endswith(".webp") and importer.IMG_NAME.match(name) and importer.IMG_NAME.match("a" * 32 + ".jpg")
    assert storage.current().get("ideas/" + name) == stored
EOF

I put the pooler address back to aws-0-ap-northeast-1. Your .env had aws2-…, which isn't a real address, and I tested aws-1-… as the alternative.

Supabase answered differently on each address:

  • aws-1-ap-northeast-1: "tenant not found", so your project isn't on that one.
  • aws-0-ap-northeast-1: it recognised the project and then rejected the login several times. That is what triggered the temporary block, so the project is on aws-0.

So the address and the project name are right, and the database password is wrong. I can't fix this one myself, because the password isn't stored anywhere I can see.

What you need to do 1. In Supabase, open Project Settings → Database → Reset database password. 2. Choose a password with only letters and digits, so it needs no special handling. 3. Put it in .env between the : and the @ in DATABASE_URL, with no brackets.

Once you've done that, tell me. I'll rerun the check, and I'll create the tables and test the full app against your Supabase straight away. A check I started earlier is still waiting to run once with the old password. It will probably fail, so ignore that result.

def _encode_password(url: str) -> str:
    """Passwords are pasted raw, but a URL needs special characters (% @ / # [ ] ...) percent-encoded.
    A password whose every % is already a valid escape (%25, %40 ...) is taken as encoded; otherwise it is literal."""
    m = _URL.match(url.strip())
    if not m:
        return url
    pw = m.group("pw")
    literal = bool(re.search(r"%(?![0-9A-Fa-f]{2})", pw)) or not re.search(r"%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}", pw)
    if literal:
        pw = quote(pw, safe="")
    else:   # already encoded: still encode anything that is not allowed, but leave the escapes alone
        pw = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._~%-]", lambda c: quote(c.group(0), safe=""), pw)
    return f"{m.group('scheme')}://{m.group('user')}:{pw}@{m.group('rest')}"


def clean_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Hosting dashboards add vendor query parameters (e.g. `supa=base-pooler.x`) that libpq rejects."""
    parts = urlsplit(_encode_password(url))''')

def test_a_password_with_special_characters_is_pasted_raw_and_still_works():

"""Copy what you already have on this computer (data/gift.db and data/photos) into your Supabase project.

   ./run.sh migrate            copy (safe to repeat: rows and photos that already exist are left alone)

Needs DATABASE_URL, SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY. Nothing is deleted or changed locally."""
import mimetypes
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
from app import config, storage  # noqa: E402
from app.db.database import DB, SCHEMA  # noqa: E402
from app.db import pg  # noqa: E402

if not (config.DATABASE_URL and config.SUPABASE_URL and config.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY):
    sys.exit("DATABASE_URL, SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY must be set (see DEPLOY.md).")
if not config.DB_PATH.exists():
    sys.exit(f"No local database at {config.DB_PATH}: nothing to copy.")

src = sqlite3.connect(config.DB_PATH)
src.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
dst = DB.open()
tables = pg.parse_schema(SCHEMA)
ORDER = ["materials", "tools", "makers", "maker_skills", "recipients", "recipient_prefs", "price_table", "ideas", "gifts",
         "creations", "skill_estimates", "technique_stats", "idea_images", "photo_analyses", "difficulty_feedback",
         "agent_runs", "motifs_dynamic", "occasions", "plans", "shown_log", "settings"]
SKIP_SETTINGS = {"seed_hash", "schema_version"}
assert set(ORDER) == set(tables), set(tables) ^ set(ORDER)

for t in ORDER:
    cols = tables[t]["cols"]
    have = {r[1] for r in src.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({t})")}
    use = [c for c in cols if c in have]
    rows = [tuple(r[c] for c in use) for r in src.execute(f"SELECT {','.join(use)} FROM {t}")]
    if t == "ideas":
        rows = [r for r in rows if r[use.index("source_type")] != "curated"]      # the curated ones come from the seed files
    if t == "settings":
        rows = [r for r in rows if r[0] not in SKIP_SETTINGS]
    if not rows:
        continue
    before = dst.conn.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM {t}").fetchone()["n"]
    dst.conn.executemany(f"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO {t}({','.join(use)}) VALUES({','.join('?' * len(use))})", rows)
    after = dst.conn.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM {t}").fetchone()["n"]
    if tables[t]["has_id"]:       # rows came with their ids: move the counter past them
        dst.conn.execute(f"SELECT setval(pg_get_serial_sequence('{config.DB_SCHEMA}.{t}', 'id'), "
                         f"(SELECT COALESCE(MAX(id), 1) FROM {config.DB_SCHEMA}.{t}))")
    print(f"  {t:20s} {len(rows):4d} local rows, {after - before:4d} added ({after} in Supabase)")

store = storage.SupabaseStorage(config.SUPABASE_URL, config.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, config.STORAGE_BUCKET)
files = [p for p in config.PHOTOS_DIR.rglob("*") if p.is_file()]
added = 0
for p in files:
    key = p.relative_to(config.PHOTOS_DIR).as_posix()
    if not store.exists(key):
        store.put(key, p.read_bytes(), mimetypes.guess_type(p.name)[0] or "image/jpeg")
        added += 1
print(f"  photos               {len(files):4d} local files, {added:4d} uploaded")
print("\nDone. Your local files were not changed.")
EOF

def clean(t):

    """Small markdown renderer: code fences, headings, bold, inline code, lists, paragraphs."""
    out=[];lines=t.split('\n');i=0;lst=None
    def inline(s):
        s=html.escape(s)
        s=re.sub(r'`([^`]+)`',r'<code>\1</code>',s)
        s=re.sub(r'\*\*([^*]+)\*\*',r'<strong>\1</strong>',s)
        s=re.sub(r'\[([^\]]+)\]\((https?://[^)\s]+)\)',r'<a href="\2" target="_blank" rel="noopener">\1</a>',s)
        return s
    def close():
        nonlocal lst
        if lst: out.append(f'</{lst}>'); lst=None
    while i<len(lines):

        if ln.startswith('```'):
            close();j=i+1;buf=[]
            while j<len(lines) and not lines[j].startswith('```'): buf.append(lines[j]);j+=1
            out.append('<pre><code>'+html.escape('\n'.join(buf))+'</code></pre>');i=j+1;continue
        if m:=re.match(r'^(#{1,4})\s+(.*)',ln):

        elif m:=re.match(r'^\s*[-*]\s+(.*)',ln):
            if lst!='ul': close();out.append('<ul>');lst='ul'
            out.append(f'<li>{inline(m.group(1))}</li>')
        elif m:=re.match(r'^\s*\d+[.)]\s+(.*)',ln):
            if lst!='ol': close();out.append('<ol>');lst='ol'
            out.append(f'<li>{inline(m.group(1))}</li>')
        elif ln.strip()=='' : close()
        else: close();out.append(f'<p>{inline(ln)}</p>')
        i+=1
    close();return '\n'.join(out)

  • Layout: each prompt appears as "Turn N". Below it is a collapsed "Claude's response" box that you click to open. Expand all and Collapse all buttons sit at the top.
  • What's in it: 68 turns, from your first "read SPEC.md…" prompt to this request. Each response box holds only my written replies, not the tool calls or file edits.

  • Gaps: a few short prompts aren't in the log as typed messages, so they're missing. These include "no emails for now" and your last question about running locally and then on Vercel. Some turns show "No written reply" because I only did tool work.
  • Duplicates: two prompts show up twice (turns 25–26 and turns 66–67) because they were sent twice.

The file may include your pasted terminal output, which can contain hostnames and the like, so check it before sharing. It also contains no secret values, as far as I know. I haven't committed it.

@router.post("/motifs/discover")
def discover_motifs(d: DiscoverIn, r: HttpRequest):
    rec = db(r).get("recipients", d.recipient_id)
    if not rec:
        raise HTTPException(404, "unknown recipient")
    rc = ctxmod.request_context(d.occasion, d.season, rec.get("relationship", ""), rec.get("age_group", "adult"))
    return motif_discovery.discover(db(r), llm(r), occasion=rc["occasion"], season=rc["season"],

def _fallback(db: DB, why: str, recipient_id, maker_id, occasion: str, message: str) -> dict:
    """No Gemini (no key, budget used up, offline): the same rules, without the model's conversation."""
    out = {"reply": why, "suggestions": [], "questions": [], "actions": [], "fallback": True}
    res = pipeline.suggest(db, Request(recipient_id=recipient_id or 0, maker_id=maker_id or 0, occasion=occasion), None, use_llm=False)
    out["suggestions"] = res["suggestions"]
    out["reply"] += " Meanwhile, here are ideas picked by the built-in rules."
    return out


def list_crafts(ctx: RunContext[Deps], maker_id: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """Crafts this maker can do with what they own (age, skill, restricted tools and inventory already applied)."""
    _, mk = _ids(ctx.deps, None, maker_id)
    if not mk:
        return {"error": "no maker selected"}
    r = pipeline.craft_options(ctx.deps.db, mk)

_init_lock = threading.Lock()


def init_state(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Open the database and build the helpers, once. Called at start-up and, as a safety net, on the first request:
    some serverless hosts never run the ASGI start-up step."""
    with _init_lock:
        if getattr(app.state, "ready", False):
            return
        app.state.db = DB.open()  # read at start-up, so tests can point it at a temp file
        app.state.db.backfill_motif_crafts(lambda m, pool: pairing.assign_crafts(m, pairing.static_motifs() + pool))
        app.state.guard = QuotaGuard(app.state.db)
        # hosted Gemini (free tier) when a key is set; the old local model client only as a fallback
        app.state.llm = GeminiClient(guard=app.state.guard) if config.GEMINI_API_KEY else LLMClient()
        app.state.jobs = Jobs(app.state.db, app.state.llm)
        # load the model in the background so the first real request is not a cold start (no threads outlive a serverless call)
        if not config.SERVERLESS:
            threading.Thread(target=lambda: app.state.llm.available() and app.state.llm.warm_up(), daemon=True).start()
        app.state.ready = True

    pat=re.compile(r'<<<<<<< HEAD\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n',re.S)
    it=iter(picks)
    def f(m):
        return next(it)(m.group(1),m.group(2))
    s=pat.sub(f,s); open(path,'w').write(s)

async def _revalidate(request, call_next):
    # local app: always re-check pages and scripts so a stale cached file cannot break the page
    resp = await call_next(request)
    path = request.url.path
    if path.startswith("/photos"):
        resp.headers["Cache-Control"] = "public, max-age=86400"          # a picture's file name never changes: no need to ask again
    elif not path.startswith("/api"):
        resp.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-cache"                       # pages and scripts: check (a 304 is quick) so edits show at once
    return resp

class OccasionIn(BaseModel):

    force: bool = False

    time_available: int | None = None
    must_use: list[str] = []
    avoid: list[str] = []


@router.post("/occasion/ideas")
def occasion_ideas(d: OccasionIn, r: HttpRequest):
    """Fetch (and cache) occasion-specific ideas. Slow on a cold occasion, instant after; the page calls it in the background."""
    rec, maker = db(r).get("recipients", d.recipient_id), db(r).get("makers", d.maker_id)
    if not rec or not maker:
        raise HTTPException(404, "unknown recipient or maker")

    req = {"budget_rupees": d.budget, "minutes_available": d.time_available, "must_use": d.must_use, "avoid": d.avoid}

    crafts = []
    return occasion_mod.ensure(db(r), llm(r), maker_id=d.maker_id, occasion=rc["occasion"], season=rc["season"],

from .text import norm

CONCEPTS = {
    "animals": "cat dog puppy kitten bird horse rabbit panda bear elephant fish dolphin butterfly pet zoo wildlife",
    "pets": "cat dog puppy kitten rabbit hamster",
    "cute": "kawaii plush teddy toy",
    "flowers": "rose lotus tulip floral bouquet blossom sunflower garden",
    "plants": "garden gardening succulent bonsai herb leaf greenery",
    "gardening": "plant plants garden herb succulent",
    "nature": "tree forest mountain hiking outdoor leaf river camping",
    "sea": "ocean beach shell fish dolphin sailing",
    "sky": "star stars moon cloud rainbow bird",
    "space": "astronaut rocket planet galaxy star stars moon nasa",
    "travel": "map trip globe adventure passport holiday wanderlust",
    "books": "reading book novel library bookmark literature story",
    "music": "guitar piano singing song concert band kpop",
    "sports": "football cricket soccer tennis basketball badminton gym fitness running yoga",
    "cooking": "baking kitchen food chef recipe tea coffee",
    "tea": "chai coffee",
    "painting": "art artist drawing sketch canvas colour color watercolor",
    "art": "painting drawing sketch artist creative design",
    "minimalism": "minimal simple clean plain",
    "colorful": "colourful rainbow bright vibrant",
    "cosy": "cozy warm blanket comfort",
    "traditional": "ethnic heritage culture classic indian",
    "photos": "photography photo picture memories album",
    "eco friendly": "sustainable recycle recycled zero waste green",
    "elegant": "classy luxury sophisticated refined",
    "sentimental": "romantic memories nostalgic emotional",
    "relaxing": "calm meditation spa wellness mindful",
    "self care": "spa skincare wellness pamper",
    "home decor": "interior decor home house room",
    "good luck": "lucky charm fortune",
}


def _stem(w: str) -> str:
    return norm(w)


def expand(likes: list[str], vocab: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    """Tags (from `vocab`, all normalised) that a recipient's free-text likes point to."""
    out: set[str] = set()
    for like in likes:
        n = _stem(like)
        words = set(n.split())
        if n in vocab:
            out.add(n)
        for tag in vocab:
            if tag in n.split() or (len(n) > 3 and (n in tag.split())):
                out.add(tag)
        for tag, hints in CONCEPTS.items():
            t = norm(tag)
            if t in vocab and (n in {norm(h) for h in hints.split()} or words & {norm(h) for h in hints.split()}):
                out.add(t)
    return out


COLOUR_WORDS = set("red pink purple blue green yellow orange white black gold silver brown grey gray violet teal maroon navy beige pastel rainbow".split())


def split(likes: list[str], materials: set[str] = frozenset()) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    """-> (interests, palette). Colours and craft materials ("pink", "ribbons") say how something looks or what it is made of,
    never what the gift IS, so they must not become the subject of an idea; topics ("cats", "football") may."""
    mats = {norm(m) for m in materials}
    topics, palette = [], []
    for like in likes:
        n = norm(like)
        words = set(n.split())
        (palette if (words & {norm(c) for c in COLOUR_WORDS}) or n in mats or n in {"ribbon", "yarn", "paper", "beads", "glitter", "fabric", "clay"} else topics).append(like)
    return topics, palette

@router.post("/recipients/default")
def default_recipient(r: HttpRequest):

You can now search for ideas without adding a recipient or a maker, and it's committed and pushed to origin/master. I ran the tests on SQLite and on a real Postgres, and all 263 pass on each. I also checked a guest search against your Supabase database. It returned ideas in about 4.7 s, and the crafts list loaded too.

What changed - Ideas page: both dropdowns now start with "Just ideas (no recipient)" and "Just ideas (no maker)". If you have no profiles yet, a small note says adding them is optional. - Without a recipient: ideas are tuned to what most people like on that occasion, with no allergy or taste filters. The existing "Default profile" does the same thing. - Without a maker: the app assumes an adult with no tool restrictions and no recorded skills. - What still needs a profile: "Card message" needs a recipient. "Plan this" and "We gave this" need both a recipient and a maker, so those buttons are hidden until you pick them. - Wrong ids: a recipient id that doesn't exist still returns an error.

The push was rejected, so I merged first origin/master had two commits I hadn't seen ("ready to deploy" and a Vercel seed-data fix), with a big redesign of the ideas page. I rebased my work on top of them without overwriting anything. Resolving that conflict meant: - Reapplying the optional-profile change to the redesigned ideas page. - Changing the redesign's picture-checking code, which still read photos from a folder, to use the new photo store. - Adding the redesign's new database columns to the Supabase tables. Your live database upgraded cleanly on restart. - Keeping the photo cache private. The redesign had set it to public. - Clearing the in-memory idea cache after an idea is edited. That fixed one test that only failed on Postgres.

Left out and still open - I left out transcript.md as before. transcript.html no longer exists, so tell me if you want it rebuilt. - Vercel will redeploy from this push. Login is still off until you set GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS, so anyone with the link can use the app. - The local app on http://localhost:8765 is restarted and running the new code.

The app isn't seeing a database URL on Vercel. Your code and Supabase are fine. The app starts up, looks for DATABASE_URL (or POSTGRES_URL) in the environment, finds neither, and stops with that error.

Likely causes, in order 1. Not redeployed: Vercel applies environment variables only to new deployments. If you added DATABASE_URL after the last deploy, go to Deployments → ⋯ on the latest → Redeploy. 2. Wrong environment: when you add the variable, tick Production (and Preview if you use preview links). A variable saved for Development only is not seen by a deployment. 3. Wrong name: it has to be exactly DATABASE_URL, with no spaces and no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix. Check for a stray space or an empty value. 4. Pasted with the label: the value must start with postgresql://. If you pasted the whole .env line, the value would begin with DATABASE_URL= and fail in a different way, not this one.

Settings → Environment Variables should list DATABASE_URL with Production ticked. If it's there, redeploy and send me the new log.

If the error comes back with the variable clearly present, tell me. I can make the error name which Supabase variables it did and didn't receive, without printing their values, so we can pinpoint it. I haven't pushed any code changes for this.

There's no .env.local in this project. The only env file is .env, and that's the one the app reads, so that's the one to copy from. The .env.example file lists the variable names but has no values.

Copying from .env into Vercel 1. Open .env in your editor and copy the DATABASE_URL line. Use the whole value after the =, without any surrounding quotes. 2. In Vercel, go to Settings → Environment Variables → Add. Put the name DATABASE_URL in the Key box and the value in the Value box. 3. Tick Production, save, then redeploy. 4. Do the same for NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY.

Vercel's "Import .env" button also works. Open the Environment Variables page and paste the contents of .env straight into the Key field, and it splits them into rows. That also pulls in the unrelated secrets in your .env, so delete those rows before saving.

I haven't printed any values here and won't. Only you should copy them from the file.

def _either(names: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
    """Process environment first (hosting dashboards), then .env."""
    return _first(*names) or next((_hosted[n] for n in names if _hosted.get(n)), "")


DATABASE_URL = _either(("DATABASE_URL", "POSTGRES_URL"))
SUPABASE_URL = _either(("SUPABASE_URL", "NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL")).rstrip("/")
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY = _either(("SUPABASE_ANON_KEY", "NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY"))

_auth_flag = os.getenv("GIFT_AUTH") or _hosted.get("GIFT_AUTH", "")
SESSION_SECRET = os.getenv("GIFT_SESSION_SECRET") or _hosted.get("GIFT_SESSION_SECRET", "") or SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY
# Creating accounts from the login page is off unless asked for: whoever knows an allowed e-mail could otherwise register it first.
ALLOW_SIGNUP = (os.getenv("GIFT_ALLOW_SIGNUP") or _hosted.get("GIFT_ALLOW_SIGNUP", "")) == "1"

79abaa8 fix: accept a DATABASE_URL pasted with surrounding quotes

Found the cause. The DATABASE_URL in Vercel has literal double quotes around it, so the app saw "postgresql://…" with the quotes included and rejected it. The app now strips quotes and stray spaces from the Supabase variables. I committed this as 79abaa8 and all 264 tests pass.

It isn't pushed yet. Do you want me to push it? Vercel can only redeploy once it's on GitHub. You can also remove the quotes from the value in Vercel's settings, and then no code change is needed.

The other error The cannot import name 'vc_handler' line belongs to the same failure. It comes from Vercel's own launcher, which prints it after the app failed to start. I expect it to go away once the database connects. If it's still there on the next deploy, I'll look at it separately.

Passwords in logs Your full database password appeared in the log you pasted to me. It's in the log lines and in this chat, so I'd change it once everything works. In Supabase, go to Project Settings → Database and reset the password, then update DATABASE_URL in both .env and Vercel. The app handles passwords with % or other special characters.

The .env line you highlighted is a Supabase secret key. I haven't repeated it. Keep it out of anything you paste.

Turn 72

what is GIFT ALLOWED EMAILS? for ?
Claude's response

GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS is the list of email addresses allowed to log in to your app. Setting it turns the login page on.

What it does - Empty or not set (your situation now): there is no login. Anyone who opens your Vercel link can see and change your recipients, allergies, makers and photos. - Set to one or more emails: every page and every photo requires a sign-in. Only the listed addresses can get in, and everyone else is turned away.

How to use it 1. In Vercel, add a variable named GIFT_ALLOWED_EMAILS. Its value is your email, raisinghani.palak@gmail.com. For several people, separate the emails with commas, with no quotes. 2. Redeploy. 3. Create your account once by running ./run.sh supabase raisinghani.palak@gmail.com on your machine. This makes the Supabase user and sets a password. After that you sign in on the app's login page.

Public sign-up is off by default. Nobody can create an account on the login page unless you also set GIFT_ALLOW_SIGNUP=1, so leave that alone.

The .env line you selected is your full database URL, including the password. Don't paste it anywhere public. It doesn't affect the login question.

You can skip all of this while you're just testing, but turn it on before sharing the link.
